Placing his pistol on the table between her and the men, her eyes finally break contact with the concrete flooring, darting directly to the gun barrel. She swallows down her emotions and takes a deep breath. Moving her handcuffed hands back up to the table in clenched fists, she opened her mouth again to say something.

"...I. I saw his face. It took me a moment, but I knew I had seen his eyes before." She stared away into space momentarily before one of the officers slammed his palm onto the table, signaling her to keep it together. She returned to reality at that moment and continued, "And it all came back to me. Who he was, what he'd done. Murdered my sister just for fun." She stopped again, tightening her eyes to force every muscle in her eyelids to hold the tears back. The officers, keeping up their stoic gazes, didn't move a muscle.

"He killed her! He mutilated her! I had to! No-no one does that and gets away! He made a mistake letting me go–I drove that knife in that bastard's throat! Dead! Dead!" Her nose flared, tears rolled down her cheeks and onto the table. She was breathing hard, her eyes were full of rage, yet her face was of sheer terror. It was as if the officers were witnessing a person, metaphorically, splitting apart at the seams.

The officers looked at one another, then returned to her enraged gaze with still emotionless faces. "Here's what you'll do. From now on, if anyone asks, it never happened. If you need to say something to anyone–and I mean, anyone–you keep your mouth shut."[Change Later]

options.name: Don't ask. Don't tell.

title: A Youth’s Mission
desc:
Young Misha was one of many in the trucks driving towards the frontlines towards the Great Trial. He was half-awake, only conscious because of the faint roars of gunfire and aircraft fighting to protect his country. A group of scary men in black uniforms had taken him and so many other people his age into bellowing trucks. He knew that the Great Trial had started so long ago, and that his family: his father, mother, and brothers, were all sent to factories or to fight the Teuton. He remembered those frightening men making big speeches, about “obedience” and “the Trial”, things that he learned in school so willingly along with his friends in their cadre.

He remembered the days in the camp where he was forced to practice fighting for the Trial. Even if the weapons he got were too heavy, he learned to show no mercy towards the Teutons who came and destroyed their homes and took away their people. Misha was confused though for he, and many other children with him were beaten and forced to struggle to live while training. He was a Russian, not an evil Teuton, why must he face beatings as if he was a criminal? Even as he ate his last meal before the black uniformed men shoveled his cadre back into the trucks, he contemplated this same question endlessly.

But these thoughts were irrelevant now; the Great Trial was now, and he had to wake up! He exited the truck, and saw his friends in his cadre and a multitude of others exit the motorized column, reforming into their companies. He saw the grown soldiers, and was inspired by their discipline and weapons. Misha emulated the others, and joined with his cadre. He saw a big man with a special suit walk in front of them, and Misha heard the suited-man proudly talk about the soldiers, including the “Black League Children Authority” battalion amongst the multitudes. He was ready, he was ready to serve his nation, and with an “URA!” in a flood of ten thousands, Misha followed his sergeant into battle with a double-time sprint!

He followed, screaming at the top of his lungs, until he took in his first sight of the battlefield. His charge into the fray steadily slowed as he saw the field of corpses and blazing fire, wide and expanding. He saw fellow Black League children lifeless amongst the wrecks of armoured vehicles and aircraft, and he was reminded of his brothers who disappeared months before. His knees began to shake. He had wanted to fight for Russia’s vengeance, not this slaughter! But words quietly forced out of his mouth, “I will be the sword and shield of Russia by which justice shall be done.” Misha screamed one last warcry, before regaining pace with his squad on the plains.

options.name: They shall not die old.

title: What's Left?
desc:
Sighing, Vyacheslav looked down at his watch. He let twenty seconds tick away before he pounded on the door for the third time. Again, nothing.

Around him, his comrades passed from door to door, knocking with gloved fists and inviting themselves inside, much to the displeasure of the unsuspecting residents. Most of them didn’t show their displeasure however; submission was a skill they had learned long ago. They sat quietly, listening to the faint murmur of the radio and sipping cups of lukewarm tea, while tall men in dark clothing tore into their apartments. They exited down the spiralling stairwell into the night, hauling loads of mismatched rifles and ancient ammunition. Vyacheslav was shocked to find so many guns, simply lying around, unused and forgotten.

“Out of the way, comrade citizen,” he grunted and pushed the old crone aside after she finally opened her door, “Official business.”

“Official?” She buzzed around him like a fly around a corpse, “I’m a Black League lady, truly. What could the Army want with me?”

“Are there any firearms on the premises, comrade citizen?”

“Well, I’m not certain I understand.”

Her hesitation was enough to tell Vyacheslav what he needed to know. Without another word, he stormed forwards, almost tearing the door off a cupboard. Shoving aside all manner of useless trinkets, his fingers slowly worked towards the back of the cupboard. All the while, the lady was making noise in his ears about her property or her rights. Vyacheslav didn’t care to listen.

He let out a wry chuckle when he noticed the rifle was still loaded. An old Mosin, unused for decades, from the Civil War if he was to judge. He pitied the poor sod at the front who would end up using this piece of shit. A quick glance was all he needed to know that this thing would jam like a bitch. Still, orders were orders, and the Great Trial came before all else. If even a single bullet from this gun found its way into German flesh, it would be worth it. The old lady stared open-mouthed at him as he left.

options.name: Everything for the front!

title: Ersatz Blitzkrieg
desc:
Vasily’s heart screamed as his fingers fumbled with the gearstick. Under his foot, the accelerator roared and spluttered, desperately trying to pull the vehicle out of the muddy pit. As he tried to climb out, Vasily pushed all of his weight into a door that refused to open. Falling back, he realized that he was going to die here.

Before he resigned himself to his fate, he dropped a gear on the old truck. The rusty metal skirts and the ridiculous cannon that had been clumsily fitted to it were weighing him down immensely, but the tyres were sturdy and designed for the wilds of Russia. He pushed the truck as hard as he could, until he felt it lurching awkwardly forward. When he finally felt the wheel press onto a rock of some kind, the engine roared triumphantly and slowly began to drag itself out of the quagmire.

As Vasily reemerged, he almost laughed at what an obscene sight it must have been, The truck’s wheels had been covered by scrap metal, crudely shaped to look like armored skirts. Along the body of the truck, sandbags held down even more of the pathetic armor that covered the truck, fastened with all manner of chains and ropes. Finally, a squat turret from the Great Patriotic War sat above the cabin. Now that the whole thing was covered in black mud, it would have been barely recognisable.

When the ‘tank’ finally came to a grunting halt, Vasily crawled out of the cabin through the back. Feeling the solid ground beneath him, his legs turned to water, struggling to hold up his weight. As he backed away from the tank, he felt sick at the thought of a creature like this facing down an infamous German panzer.

Before Vasily could speak, the captain turned and glanced briefly at the pathetic tank.

“It’ll do nicely,” Vasily heard the captain say to his colleagues. “I want as many as you can get me ready for the end of the week.”

Vasily rose to his feet, shaking his fist and yelling.

“You think that piece of shit is going to stand up to a German tank? The drivers will be dead before they even reach the front!”

With the ground still shaking beneath his feet, he strode angrily towards the captain. Before he could say anything else, an aide grabbed him by the arm, and the captain issued a single command.

options.name: “He’s in shock. Get him to the infirmary.”

title: A Quivering Plea
desc:
[Change Later]"Dmitry Yazov stared at the document which lay in front of him with both a feeling of utter shock and an equally strong urge to break into a fit of cackling. He almost couldn't believe his eyes as he read the address.

"To the Glavkoverkh of the great Russian nation,

I'm sure you are under no misconceptions that the war between our two states has devolved into needless and total death and destruction. I know you do not wish for your people to suffer any more than I do mine. I urge you, please, reopen communication between our two governments. This war does not have to end in the manner I dread to imagine you believe it does. We can find a way to avoid any further destruction and find a path to peace.

Please,

The Office of the Fuhrer of the Greater Germanic Reich"

Yazov read through the letter again with nothing short of complete awe. That bastard even put his own little signature at the end. What did they expect to come of this wailing cry to save their own skins? A peace? He couldn't help a small chuckle escape his mouth. They must be more desperate than he thought. This pathetic appeal to escape Russia's rightful retribution was all the proof Yazov needed that the Trial was truly bringing an end to the Teutonic fever dream of Aryan supremacy. The great Russian Spirit had to be prevailing, or else they wouldn't resort to such lowly begging.

Still, he supposed a response was in order. His secretary dictated his words as they left his tongue without a moment of hesitation or thought.

"To the Fuhrer of the German cancer which stains Europe,

We will have peace once every last wretched German man, woman, and child lies in a ditch with the flag of the Black League waving over their corpses. I will hang your rotten body myself when I arrive at the shattered remains of Berlin.

Signed,

Dmitry Yazov, Glavkoverkh of the Russian Black League"[Change Later]

options.name: The only response was deafening radio silence.

title: Military Grade
desc:
Leonid felt life returning to his frozen fingers as he shakily poured three cups of tea. He and the other two were crowded around a makeshift campfire, savoring the warmth and calm after days of endless battle. Two days ago, they had finally been pulled from the frontlines, but Leonid knew the officers weren’t pleased in the slightest. Every inch of soil they had fought and bled for had been lost, after it became clear that no-one had the strength, or even the weapons to continue. And so, they had huddled behind the front for the past few days in silence, waiting for fresh meat and guns to arrive.

When the soldiers were called to assemble, Leonid knew that it wasn’t good. Quickly draining the last fiery drops of his tea, he joined the mindless river of men shuffling towards the senior officers. As expected, Leonid spied huge crates being unloaded from trucks and opened, to reveal the guns within. The men already assembled must have been the newest recruits sent to fill the gaps. Leonid snorted. Not one of them looked a day over sixteen.

Even as the officers were announcing a renewed offensive, a murmur rose through the crowd of soldiers. It was a moment before Leonid noticed that none of the weapons presented looked to have been made this decade. Hell, some of them probably hadn’t seen service since the First World War. From ceremonial Tsarist guns to shotguns taken from a film set, the cache would have been better suited for a museum than a war. Hesitantly, a few soldiers began slowly making their way towards the weapons.

“I suppose it’s better than nothing,” Leonid muttered, reaching down. As he placed his hand on the barrel of a rifle, he felt another hand on his shoulder. Looking over, he saw a brutish officer staring down at him disapprovingly.

“Comrade medic, these rifles are for soldiers, not nurses.”

“For soldiers? I’ve seen more of the front than any of those kids you’ve recruited straight out of kindergarten.”

“What I mean to say, comrade medic, is that a rifle is worth more in the hands of a killer, not a doctor. You can choose from the weapons over there.”

As Leonid looked over to where the man was pointing, he felt his throat tighten. His legs almost gave out beneath him as he shuffled towards a crate filled with wooden poles, carved in the shape of rifles.

options.name: As long as the enemy thinks it’s real.

title: Echo In The Wind
desc:
Anatoly scratched the bottom of the hood covering his gas mask, exterminating a scorching itch that plagued him since the start of the patrol. Today was nothing but another daily march. Their objective: crush the embers of Teuton partisan activity in the Volga settlements. He couldn’t stand the monotony. It frustrated him to enter empty villages and ersatz graveyards without the Russian praise or Teutonic slaughter that he was promised. Still, his duty was to obey, and he kept marching.

Anatoly's squad leader, Sergeant Petrovich, raised his hand; they'd reached their destination. It was a scorched village, an empty cairn that housed dozens of traitorous Volga dogs. The Sergeant’s orders were simple, to keep together and to keep patrolling for ambushers.

Moments turned to minutes, nearly into hours. But what did he find? Nothing but the whistle of the wind through bones and the crackling of embers. There was nothing here, just like all the other villages. That feeling of unfulfillment kept crawling into his skin, then into his mind, worse than any itch. It scuttled and burrowed, tormenting him, driving him mad. Anatoly couldn’t handle it any longer. His duty was to force the Teutons out of their burrows, but what was he doing here? Wasting time, just like every other day!

“Come out, you rats!" he screamed. "Come out so I can kill you!”

Anatoly felt the butt of a rifle jam into his chest and two hands grab his collar. The Sergeant was livid. “Private Dyushev, you fucking idiot! Don’t you know that there are partisans?” The voice of the sergeant echoed through the square like Anatoly’s taunts.

The sergeant could only hear the fading echoes booming through the air, then; nothing. Likewise, his anger faded and was replaced with the same feeling; the terror of unfulfillment and fatigue that Anatoly had just outburst over. The sergeant let go of Anatoly and shook his head in resignation.

“Don’t you dare tell anyone about this incident.”

options.name: What good are soldiers if there’s nothing to fight?

title: Those Who Fought For Love
desc:
Pavel had simple orders from the Black League: call the partisans in this village to fight against the Teuton. He was trained to fulfill this one order, and he carried it out wholeheartedly in the early stages of the Great Trial. He knew these partisans and he knew this village for they were like family to him. Months ago, he remembered everything about them, and grew to love them beyond their patriotism: their hospitality to him, their camaraderie, their total resolve in years fighting against the Teuton. It was a shame to Pavel that the Glazoverkh denounced Communists as decadent and Muscovites as irredeemable, if only the Glazoverkh knew who those Partisans really were.

Regardless, there was a mission to complete, and it started in the village. The moment he took his first step, he knew that by the time he returns back to his seniors, they’ll have him shot.

Pavel forced himself to continue walking, scanning the bombed roads and the husks of peoples’ homes and livelihoods, torn by warfare. He could only hear the howls of the cold winds and the rustling and crumbling of the debris which covered it. It took him only ten minutes to find what he was looking for; an unassuming store. Pavel entered quickly and immediately walked to the back of the store, his eyes pointed at the backroom storage door. He knew that all it took was two words, before he could meet their smiling faces once again.

“Krasnaya Armiya”

Minutes passed, and there was no response. Pavel entered the room, and went down to its basement, but he only found it abandoned. He felt a lump in his throat, and continued forwards.

He entered the Partisans’ planning room, where he got to meet Western Russia’s quiet defenders, but he only saw the smears of long-dried blood, and casings: Mauser and IzhMash. He couldn’t even see any bodies, but he knew that the people that he called comrades, the people who loved him like their son, were gone forever. Pavel picked up one of their armbands, red star painted, and gripped it in sorrow.

The Red Partisans were the closest to his heart, and he could never replace them with anyone in the Black League. So Pavel shoved the armband in his coat pocket, and set off to return back to his officers, no matter what awaited him.

options.name: He wanted to return home, to meet his comrades once again.

title: Our Eternal War
desc:
They all swarmed around him like vultures as he sat patiently behind the desk. Slowly, the world wrapped its fangs around him, as the lights snapped on, the microphone began to crackle and the cameras began rolling. As an aide slid a single sheet of paper in front of him, his vision blurred and the letters swum. After choking back the bile in the back of his throat, Yazov’s eyes snapped open and once again, he spoke.

“Comrade Russians. The Great Trial marches ever onward. Every day, the Motherland swells with pride to know that all brave sons of Russia have answered the call, and now march on a holy war to annihilate the German parasite. With every inch of stolen soil reclaimed, the honour of Russia is restored.

However, an ugly beast has once again reared its head. The spectre of defeatism. Not by any fault of men at the front, but by the insidious plotting of cowards in the dark, the Great Trial grinds to a halt. They deceive true Russians with their honeyed words, claiming our war is futile, even cruel. Such creatures are as detestable as the collaborator, scarcely a step above a German, as they aim to break the Russian spirit itself. Be vigilant, comrade Russians, for it is your duty as Russians to expose these traitors and stave off their lies. A noose has been tied for each and every renegade, awaiting only their necks.

And remember, comrade Russians, this is the war that has always been. From Aleksandr Nevsky to Tsar Nikolai, the plains of Russia have been marked by the shadow of our struggle against the German dogs, as this war passed through generations. Even after swallowing bitter defeats without end, the Red Armies of Bukharin and Voroshilov gave their blood and tears to Russian soil, against a thunderstorm of steel and fire, before passing the torch of war to us.”

Yazov’s brow hardened as he leaned into the microphone, slamming his fist on the desk as he spoke the final words.

“Russia has always fought this war, and will continue to fight it. The Great Trial is all that there has ever been. If it takes ten years, or ten thousand, every inch of German flesh shall rot beneath our triumphant boots.”

options.name: Forevermore.

title: Misgiven Trust
desc:
Adrian Volkov hurriedly stepped into the town square of the village, recently liberated by the Black League. The streets were entirely empty, no one in the small settlement had left their homes since the last Wehrmacht company abandoned the town. Adrian figured they were likely too scared to even notice the lifting of the jackboot from their necks. He walked along the desolate street in a stern, speedy gait, entirely alone but moving with the same vigilance expected from a formal march.

He passed home after home, barely paying attention to them as he continued down the road. Finally he found a man, gathering water from a well near his house. Adrian approached, the silence in the streets accentuating the clacking of his boots against the stone beneath him.

"Comrade! I was hoping you could help me with something!" As he called out to him the man seemed startled. As Adrian grew closer he pulled a photograph from his pocket and showed the villager. "I was hoping you could help me find these two," He pointed to a smiling couple with a small boy next to them. "They should be somewhere in this town, though older than in the photo of course." The man did nothing but stare. "Comrade, please, have you seen them?"

The man gazed at Adrian as he stumbled through his words. "T- Tut mir leid, ich spreche kein Russisch." Adrian stumbled backwards away from the German. His mind raced. Why was a Teuton civilian here? Then, for the first time since entering the town Adrian truly looked at the buildings around him. His rush-induced tunnel vision dissipated as he studied them more closely. He found German architecture and beaten crooked crosses adorning them. His face turned completely pale as the reality of what had become of his home dawned on him.

The man kept pleading, "Bitte, ich-" he was interrupted by a shot ringing out from Adrian's rifle. A woman left the house behind them and screamed at the sight. Adrian turned to face her. Inside he could see a portrait of Hitler adorning the mantle. He again aimed his rifle and shot, his eyes entirely cold and lifeless.

The cracks ringing through the village wouldn't end until well past midnight.

options.name: Vengeance, at the cost of his soul.

title: Minesweepers
desc:
Klara scanned the line of fellow prisoners who had joined her. Most of them carried the bloodied marks of torture, all of them were withered beyond belief. She was no exception. Some were old enough to be her grandfather. Many were young enough to be her children. If it weren’t for the weeks of sleeplessness, hunger, and pain, she would’ve burst into tears then and there. Instead, she turned back towards the sergeant. A well built, intimidating man with a penchant for suffering, he made the perfect leader of this “internment facility” for captured Germans like herself. And with a sadistic smile, he began to address his most hated subjects...

“Teuton scum! We are here today to offer you something. You see, although you are all worthless and evil now, the Black League believes that anyone can achieve redemption. Now, we will determine who is worthy of it. You see that hill in the distance? Anyone who makes it to the top will be released from here and enlisted into the army immediately. There is one... small issue, however.” The smile on his face grew larger. “...There’s a minefield in the way, and I don’t know where the mines are.”

Klara’s soul shattered. She had expected to die here, but not like this. Anything but this. As her innards writhed in agony, the demonic creature standing before her continued...

“That’s where you come in. Make it through the field and earn your freedom. If you don’t, well, that’s just one less mine I need to worry about. Anyone who does not walk forward on my command will be shot. Oh, and if you don’t mind, we’ll be recording your “valiant” redemption for all the world to see. Ready!...”

Klara wanted to run away, to scream, to cry, to fall over, to do something, anything, that would prevent, even stall her fate. But she couldn’t. She had heard what happened to people who tried to defy the League. It was one of the few things that still sickened her. All she could do, with the hill in her eyes and the sergeant’s cackles in her ears, was walk forward...

“...March!”

options.name: ...and hope for a painless death.

title: Battle on the Ice
desc:
[Change Later]"The brackish waters of Lake Peipus lapped gently at the sandy loam beneath the Glavkoverkh's feet. They were a disappointment. Polluted with industrial runoff and garbage, the lake stank of rotting fish and urine; plastic bags and rotting food collected in the grass at the water's edge in molding clumps.

Yazov sighed. His ears burned as the wind bit at exposed skin, and his fingers stiffened in frozen agony  within mink-fur gloves. "I shouldn't have come here." He turned to his attendant, a nameless bodyguard with a boxer's build and a missing tooth. "I've wasted the League's resources clearing a safe road for my attendance today. And for what? An indulgence." He paused, and looked back at the faecal-brown water. "Another provocation. Another sin perpetrated against our sacred motherland, against the Russian national body. I came here searching for a symbol of our history, and have found only a crime scene."

The bodyguard remained expressionless. "I'm not here to judge you, sir."

"No, I claim that duty for myself, and myself alone." Yazov snarled. "Symbols are for the weak. They are the bilious discharge of propaganda, and if our civilization was as strong as we must be in the coming days, we would reject them out of hand!" Yazov ground his teeth together. He clenched his fists, threatening to tear out the stitching of his gloves. "A great victory was won on this frozen lake, long ago. And Russian blood was shed to defend Russian civilization, before Russia called itself Russia. But in these days, every inch of our home is soaked in the blood of patriot-martyrs. To elevate one great victory only displays my own disrespectful failure to honor our comrades who completed their final duty."

Yazov turned his back on the stinking morass, and began the march back to his motorcade. "With me, comrade soldier. We will not honor Alexander Nevsky's legacy by fawning over a pool of water."

As he walked, he thought of German knights run through with spears, choking on their own blood, praying to a corpse. He thought of the Livonian Order, extinguished and replaced by Slavic settlers. And Yazov's thoughts turned to Germania."[Change Later]

options.name: Everything sacred is already exhausted, every hope extinguished.

title: The Glavkoverkh Speaks
desc:
[Change Later]"Comrade Russians, The Great Trial is upon us.

More than thirty years ago, the true path of history was altered forever. Our Motherland blossomed in the company of its people, awaiting what was to be her glorious destiny. In a just world, the Russian Eagle would perch itself above the world, gazing benevolently upon her domain and exorcising its will freely upon the World.

Then, the Führer's armies, ignited by hatred and an unstoppable thirst for blood, tore through our lands, leaving nothing but ashes and ruins in their wake. The Third Reich of Germany defiled history itself when it stole from us our sacred destiny. They tore down from Russia's people are rightful place as the Earth's Hegemon.

As a generation of Russia's people lie beneath our soul, another has risen to exact the Motherland's vengeance upon the wretched Reich. I ask of you, my sacred people, Kill! Kill for your Motherland! Count not the days that have passed you by, but by the number of German lives you have ended!

If your rifle is loaded, empty it into the enemy's chest. If your bayonet is clean, smother it with the blood of your ancestor's killers! If you possess not a weapon, then you will use your hands to rip and tear the Teuton's flesh off his bones. Use every action necessary to exact your revenge upon the Monsters of Prussia!

For those who believe they cannot take a life. For those who lack the capacity to right the great wrongs of our history, remember that If you do not kill the German Soldier, he will spare no mercy in taking your life. If you do not bury his offspring beneath the Earth, then he will massacre your children! If you do not kill his wife, she shall bear the German race on forevermore!

Know this, Comrade Russians. We have waited three decades to get our chance at reclamation. Only when the concept of "Germany" has been buried beneath the great monolith of history can our sacred Motherland know peace. From today, Comrade Russians, the Great Trial has begun! Glory to Victory! Glory to the Black League!"[Change Later]

options.name: Vengeance. Vengeance, through any means necessary.

title: A Letter Of Intent
desc:
“To the damnable government of the Greater Germanic Reich,

If you wish to avoid the destruction upon your nation which will surely be wrought by failure to comply, you will adhere to the demands which have been listed in this letter. Any response other than complete assent to our requests will be cause for immediate and total war against your abhorrent nation.

Firstly, the Black League demands the prompt return of all German Reichskommisariats in Eastern Europe which house Russian or otherwise Slavic populations to the control of the Reclamation Government to be reincorporated as territory of its administration. Any German colonizers present in these lands are expected to return to Germany within thirty six hours or face immediate execution for the raping of the lands which they occupy.

Secondly, the German Reich is to immediately and without protest present the officials currently holding any and all higher offices of its state, including that of the Fuhrer, to the Black League for immediate military tribunal. In addition, the German people must unilaterally be found as guilty of genocide and destruction of the Slavic and Russian peoples and be sentenced to pay collective reparations of at least one hundred billion Reichsmarks. Payment in full to the Russian National Reclamation Government is expected no less than ten years from today.

Furthermore, the organs of state of the German Reich are to be placed under direct control of the Russian Government for inspection of their heinous and undeniable crimes against the world and sacred Russia. Black League officials are to oversee the trial of these state organizations and their administrators.

The National Socialist German Workers Party is to be immediately disbanded and any who hold membership are to be banned from holding public office. A complete list of these rats responsible for destroying the Russian nation is to be sent to the Black League for inspection and to do with as it sees fit.

Finally, the German government is to formally and unconditionally surrender to the Black League. The full punishment of its people is to be determined by the Russian Government at a later date.

We await your response.”

options.name: “They can't be serious, can they?”

title: One More Job
desc:
Sergei was sitting with his comrades, after a long and tiring day. It was, surprisingly, a quiet week on that side of the frontline. No reports of any counter-attack by the Germans, and the General commanding his division had ordered them to dig in and defend the position until they had an opportunity to attack. Some of the lads were disappointed, but Sergei felt it was a great opportunity to relax and play some cards. They'd listen to the radio, but all that old thing could play was a transmission of Sacred War from an army station nearby, and frankly, everyone was tired of listening to that.

"Hey, you!" — Sergei heard, immediately turning his head at the sound's source. "The soldiers need you on the other side of the camp to carry a corpse. Apparently, one private there decided to kill himself."

Sergei felt annoyed. They always called him for this kind of task. He would protest, but he knew his opinion didn't matter, so he got on his feet and headed over to where the corpse was.

He was pretty much used to it at that point, but it was still a disgusting sight. The young soldier, possibly 15 to 18 years old, had shot himself with his handgun, with the bullet going through his mouth and up into his brain, apparently having fired the gun right below his chin.

Sergei really didn't have much time, and decided to drag the body to a nearby mass grave. After slightly raising him by his legs, Sergei noticed a small book falling off the corpse's pockets. He picked it up, noticing it was a diary. Sergei was intrigued, they almost never found something interesting on that side of the front. He put the diary inside his jacket's right pocket, so that he could read it later. Sergei was eager to learn about the experiences of another soldier, but he didn't have the time for it at that moment. For now, he had a corpse to carry.

After launching the corpse in that dig, reuniting him with his comrades, Sergei headed back to his friends. Night was about to fall, and he still wanted to play cards before it was too late.

options.name: Nothing matters any more

title: If You Gaze Into The Abyss...
desc:
00:53

Day 1: My name is Alexander. This is officially the beginning of my diary. Today, I have enlisted in the National Reclamation Army. I am happy to be fighting for my motherland and helping the Black League destroy the Teuton threat. Tomorrow I will be starting my military training, and hopefully, join the front lines as soon as possible. I shall make my family proud by fighting the Germans in the Great Trial. Glory to Russia, indivisible and invincible.

20:24

Day 2: Today was my first military training. We started off by doing the oath of allegiance to the Black League. It was glorious. After that, we started the drills. They were very tiring, but they are necessary, for they will turn me into the ultimate killing machine in the Great Trial. When the sun went down, the lads lit a campfire and we burned a German flag. It was a great day, but I expect to honor Russia by joining the frontlines soon.

04:36

Day 36: In the preceding days, I have finished my training and finally been sent to the frontlines, near the German border. Upon arrival at the military camp, I realized things weren't as I predicted. I was assigned to a platoon dedicated to searching newly conquered settlements and eliminating threats hiding inside places our frontline divisions couldn't afford to get into. I was disappointed, but I understand someone has to do it. For Comrade Yazov. For Russia.

23:59

Day 40: Today, I killed a German for the first time. Our platoon entered a government building to search for any possible threats, and we found two German soldiers hiding in one of the rooms. Gunfire ensued as soon as our comrades saw the Teutons. We managed to kill one of them as soon as the shootout started with three bullets in the chest. The other soldier was wounded in the leg and dropped his weapon while crawling inside another room. I ran after him and shot him. I know I did no wrong, he deserved it. After all, he was a German. He made us all suffer for so long... But as I looked into his eyes, as I saw the light fade away... I pitied him. I did the right thing. I'm sure of it. I'm helping save Russia.

options.name: “This is getting interesting.”

title: ...The Abyss Will Gaze Back
desc:
23:34

Day 47: I'm writing this right after I arrived at the camp. I don't know who else to talk to. Today, we found a family of Germans hiding in their house. I was surprised, but I didn't really think much of it. I don't know...What I did...I feel like a monster. They made me kill them. They made me shoot them all. The woman, the children...I can't take it anymore. Everytime I close my eyes, I see their faces, begging for mercy. But I had to, didn't I? I had to do it, for...For my sake. Otherwise they'd kill me too! The blood, the suffering...Out of all of them, the children were the ones who screamed louder. It was so loud. I can still hear their screams...They haven't stopped ever since we left the settlement and it's driving me insane. Am I really on the right side? They were Germans, but they were unarmed. And the children...They didn't deserve that. Maybe...They all deserved it, right? Right? May God help me.

22:53

Day 61: Today marks 2 months since I decided to join this godforsaken army. The screams have not stopped. They keep playing in my head, like a broken record. Today, we rounded up around 20 civilians, pushed them into a trench, aimed at them and held the trigger. The screams intensified after that. Every day, they seem to be getting louder, and louder...As if many people were screaming at once. I have been unable to sleep for several days, because every single time I close my eyes I see all of them. Everyone, dying by my hand. I did horrible things to innocent people. I was just following orders, wasn't I? I believe that, but the voices keep telling me I'm a monster. How is it possible that I'm hearing voices over all of this SCREAMING? Somebody help me, I can't take this anymore.

Night

Day ?: I have no idea what day it is, all I can tell is that it's night. I can't leave my tent anymore. They scare me. I see them, lurking outside, in the middle of the fields, waiting to punish me for what I have done. I have killed so many of them. The voices don't stop, they won't stop. They keep telling me it's my fault...Someone please help me, please...For whoever is reading this, don't make the same mistake I did. I will find peace in the only place I can, and find forgiveness for my sins...I'm sorry, little children. I'm sorry, Russia. And good riddance, Yazov and your filthy lies.

options.name: “I could've slept without reading this.”

title: Arise, Motherland Of Mine!
desc:
“You can’t do this,” his mother howled, “He belongs right here with me, not in some godforsaken German ditch.”

Timofey didn’t struggle as the officers seized him firmly by the arms and pulled him from his apartment. After living under Yagoda’s tyranny for most of his life, he knew better than to resist.

“Your son is a man, comrade citizen,” one of the officers, Lieutenant Chekov, was trying to explain to his mother, “He must fulfill his duty to the Motherland.”

“Look how young he is,” she sobbed, “How weak he is! He’s not even fit to hold a gun!” As if to prove her point, she started desperately hurling punches at Timofey. Before she could strike him, Chekov clamped her fist in his own.

“The Great Trial waits for no-one, comrade citizen,” Chekov explained patiently, “When the Motherland calls, we answer.”

“To hell with the Motherland!” She screamed back at him, “To hell with the Germans, the League and your Great Trial! Give me back my boy! He’s mine!”

Before Timofey could hear Chekov’s cold response, he was bundled out of the apartment and into the stairwell. As he felt the icy eastern air screaming upwards, he saw black fists beating on every door, on every level. Green boys to weathered old men were all being torn from the warmth of their bed by the Glavkoverkh’s hungry fingers, spirited away into the night by a sea of shadowy silhouettes.

As he was marched down the stairs, Timofey was herded into a stream of boys just like him. Exiting the building, they saw fat trucks, bursting with Yazov’s thugs. Rivers of black poured across the streets, wielding bright flashlights and kicking down doors with iron-shod boots.

As the boys quietly sat there, a sleek, black car emerged from the darkness, its headlights blinding them. After it came to a graceful stop, a slender figure stepped out of it, snowflakes crunching under his leather shoes. The two soldiers that remained stood to attention and saluted the general as he regarded the newest recruits with disdain. He spoke up, mentioning a name none of them had ever heard before.

options.name: “Send them to Vorkuta.”

title: Purpose in Hate
desc:
Anatoly barely remembered his home village. It was a small little place, just outside Kursk. He couldn't have been much older than five when he was forced out of his home. The only thing he truly remembered was leaving. The smell of smoke and gunpowder through every street, screams echoing from across every building. As he left the village in a crowded truck he even saw, just for a moment, the first Wehrmacht companies entering the town.

His family had escaped by the skin of their teeth, narrowly avoiding the earliest days of the Luftwaffe bombings, eventually, coming to Tomsk. Life became almost peaceful in Pasternack's Republic, but even that wouldn't last. The assault from further east once again thrust him into the middle of war, but this time he decided to remain in his home, and as the writer's state collapsed on itself and throughout the Smuta, Anatoly felt nothing but shame at his people's self-destruction.

Years later when he laid eyes on the first Black Guard unit in the streets, he felt that same contempt of the Russian people tearing themselves apart. However, that changed as he witnessed them offer the defending soldiers amnesty for a place in the League. And as his city was swiftly remade in the League's vision, slowly, Anatoly was as well.

The radio addresses he listened to spoke of nothing short of complete devotion to vengeance against the German, true unity in struggle amongst Russians. The very thing Anatoly wished for was now mandated by the will of the Glavkoverkh. He became fully devoted to the Black League and the Trial, address by address and speech by speech. His suffering fueled frustration became directed fully toward duty to the League as his heart filled with cold, unwavering rage.

He saw now that all the League had done was in the name of the Great Trial, to liberate all under the Germanic boot. The Black League's actions were not only necessary, but just. For the first time in many years Anatoly felt pride in being a Russian again. He was grateful for the newfound direction in his hatred. The Reclamation Government was fighting a sacred struggle, and he was truly thankful to be part of it.

options.name: The echoes of all that was lost ring through Russia.

title: The End Rimes
desc:
It had been several long days on the road. When word got out of the League’s plans to finally use their nuclear arsenal, everything went to shit. Entire towns emptied underground, people running for the wilds, and mass desertions. Pyotr was one such deserter, having stolen a motorcycle and jerry cans to last him through his final mad dash across Russia. He had been driving north nonstop, only stopping to eat his now-meagre rations. There was only one plan on his mind, the only possible way to get out of this ordeal alive, and with every turn of the motorcycle’s wheels, he prayed for it to all work out.

As the sun began to rise, Pyotr feared he would be too late. He began to speed up even more, his unsleeping eyes dead ahead as his destination came into view beyond the early morning fog... Arkhangelsk. He once again hoped and prayed to God, Jesus, and all the saints in the world that Andrei would be there waiting for him. He promised him, he did. He would never abandon Pyotr, he’s a good man. Even if the others wanted to leave without Pyotr, Andrei would convince them. He was a good navy man, he had sway, he had power. He had to be waiting there.

Pyotr rode into Arkhangelsk at full speed, his eyes focused only on the road as the city’s dead silence greeted him. Everyone was gone now; either to the bunkers, the wilds, or the sea. He continued down onto the docks, where the sight of a large steel vessel still docked in port made him cry tears of joy. He wiped his tears off as he got off the motorcycle, taking what was left of his meagre possessions as he ran faster than he ever did in his life to the ship. He looked up at the men on the deck, locking eyes with Andrei as a smile crossed both of their faces. The bridge quickly lowered for Pyotr as he got on, embracing Andrei and the rest of his comrades. Come hell or high water, they would be together for this one.

As the ship cast off, Pyotr tightened his coat as he looked back at his motherland. A feeling of dread overcame him, as the shore receded further and further beyond his sight. He took a deep breath and closed his eyes as sirens began to sound off in the distance, and hellfire rained.

options.name: Deign to save the suppliant soul.

title: The Liberation of Volgograd
desc:
Not many times have two armies met with such vicious hatred that the only memento of their engagement were the smoldering remains of what were once people. The ravenous hostility bursting out from the Black Army had caused them to furiously bombard the city of Volgograd without any real objective other than to rack up the highest body count as fast as possible, no matter who was on the receiving end of the strikes.

Russian forces held a small victory parade in the town square, with not a mouse cheering for their arrival. The residents of the cities held fast in dread and fear. The men of the army considered turning their guns on the civilians, but the generals decided not to waste any more bullets today. After all, there was still the march to Germania to consider, and the League was not one to waste.

As the Russians geared up for the next advance, German radio chatter flared up with panic-stricken soldiers and officers running for their lives from the Black Army, giving ghastly accounts of the horrors that they had just faced. Diplomatic cables from Ukraine and Caucasia were sending alarm signals to just about every channel within Neu Berlin that the machines receiving them were on the verge of exploding on the spot.

A terrifying trepidation silently fell across the world as all eyes were on the war. For those that listened, a realization crept into their minds, raging like the metal seas that washed over eastern europe. Perhaps...Perhaps this might be the last war. For Germany, for Russia, for the world.

options.name: No Mercy Under the black flag.

title: Ashes to Ashes
desc:
The fire burned brightly, creating a strangely comforting afterglow. Leonid Pesterev looked upon the sight with a sense of marvel. How easy it was, for a city to burn, especially one as filthy as Adolfsburg.

He watched as prisoners dressed like tattered grey effigies of the Wehrmacht ambled past towards a large hall, the remnants of a town hall. His comrades herded the scum into the hall and for those that resisted, they received a rifle butt to the face and were thrown in after.

As the last of them was shoved in, Leonid took out a molotov cocktail he had prepared earlier, as did those around him. He lit it and tossed it towards the building. The drywood caught fire quickly. He could hear the desperate wails of the filth inside the hall, it was much sturdier than it appeared to have held up against the ceaseless pounding of the damned within it.

Soon the screams stopped, the sickly smell of charred flesh wafting through the air. Leonid looked on with impassion as the flames grew brighter, flying higher as they attempted to ascend. The flames died out after several long minutes as the ashes slowly drifted down like tattered grey snow.

Leonid recalled a life long past, one where he had a family. It was good, but it was gone. He remembered the day when men in grey uniforms came to his village. He remembered the cries and screams of despair of his mother and sister as they were taken away. He remembered the all-too-familiar smell of burnt flesh as he hid under the floorboards of his burning home. He remembered.

 He could see an arm twitching amidst the pile of bodies, and he pulled away the burnt corpses to uncover it. A youth, no more than eighteen years of age was revealed, his stark blue eyes filled with fear.

“Bitt- Please, no more Kamerad, nein, NEI–”.

Leonid thrusted the bayonet through his head, it was almost effortless. He watched as the body stilled, perhaps this would have been his fate if he had not been so lucky as to escape the eyes of the rapacious Nazi scum. He looked towards the burning city, mesmerised by its collapse into ruin.

options.name: Earth to earth, ashes to ashes, dust to dust.

title: A Rude Awakening
desc:
Gotthard woke up to the blasting of bombs overhead.

It shook him out of bed and rushed him outside. Seeing the bomber fly and whizz overhead brought him back to the old days when he himself was able to do such things. The power he felt as the bomber flew through the air, wreaking havoc over the cities across the East. Of course now he was in his twilight years and wasn’t the same man he was twenty years ago.

The near constant barrage of high explosive bombs lit up the Germanic side of the city. Lighting the churches ablaze along with the markets. People inevitably were running to the air raid shelters as the haze of his mind was broken by the loudness of machine guns firing down and pelting people. He ran towards the hospital, surely they would not fire upon a building bearing the red cross.

Suddenly a large explosion almost seemed to rock the Earth, coming from the hospital. Gotthard was knocked to the ground as the glass was blasted from the hospital. It crumbled, slowly falling to the ground as the street was coated in a thick dust. Gotthard didn’t even notice that his leg was full of glass alongside most of his body.  He passed out shortly after the fact.

Waking up he felt a little better. The pain still was all around his body; however there was a sweet looking face tending to him. The kind woman took a pitcher and made a cup of what he assumed to be tea. He glanced around to see other people laying on stretchers. Gotthard gripped the glass the kind nurse gave him. “I see you still have your strength” she said as the young woman chuckled. Pouring the tea down his throat the warmth began to offset his pain with soothing peace.

options.name: It was broken by more bombs.

title: The Streets of Moscow Run Red
desc:
Gotthard woke up again, clutching a dirty kitchen knife to his side, it had been all a blur to him when the Black League invaded Moscow. Laying amongst the rubble he had to get into the sewer lines. If he could not then surely he would be captured and most likely executed there on the spot. He had seen so much in the few days he was able to walk around.

There was the looting of the German side of the city, the taking of men from their families and being rounded up. There was always the loud rang of machine gun fire after such things. But, as the occupation continued hopes were dashed that Germany would be able to mount such a counterattack against the League.

Deciding to take his chances he exited the safety the rubble had given him for a brief respite and ran towards a shell crater exposing a part of the open sewage line. Crouching into the filth and sludge filling the drainage pipe he could remember other things the occupation had given to him in those early days. The images of children being shot alongside their mothers much to the chagrin of the Black League soldiers had horrified Gotthard.

Of course he had bombed cities and towns and surely it had killed at least one person but this, this was entirely different to him. Crawling through the blood and bile filled system a flash of light grazed his face. Russian shouting began to fill the pipe as he was ordered out of the pipes.

options.name: His lucky streak had ended.

title: The Second Day of the Rope
desc:
Gotthard was in a line, not like the lines of bread his fellow Germans had wanted during a state of national emergency, Gotthard was in line to be hanged alongside an almost endless line of German men. A Black League cadre commander espousing in Russian things he could not understand. Whatever it was he was saying, there was indeed great passion under those words.

Another drop of the handle, and more men were hung.

Gotthard looked around, was everyone just going to watch this happen. Of course some were cheering and clapping merrily, but most were walking along the bombed out streets of Moscow. The man in front of him turned his head to the side and said “Hey, I’m running, want to come with?”

Another drop of the handle, and more men were hung.

“What no, surely we’d be shot” Gotthard stated rather frankly. “We are dead men already, I’m just going out on my own accord” and with that the man ran to his right only to almost instantly be rained down upon by machine gun fire. Bullets riddled the man’s corpse and he was dead before he hit the floor.

Another drop of the handle, and more men were hung

It was his turn to step towards the gallows. He walked up the makeshift steps and looked around him one last time. Finally he looked at the heavens, to see if divine fate would save him and that God himself would take pity on a man such as himself.

options.name: He dropped like the rest.

title: There Will Come Soft Fog...
desc:
Creeping its way across the sleeping city of Konigsberg was an early morning fog, blanketing the city–like a butterfly lying in wait inside its cocoon. Only the residents up before the sun witnessed the eerie, yet mesmerizing work of art created by what seemed like unearthly powers. As the fog rolled its way covering the entire city, it was only until then that the sun began to find itself creeping over the horizon, penetrating the fog with sharp beams of light–creating a sight that some would have thought was a work of God alone.

But there came a strange, eerie feeling as the fog remained hovering amongst the city. As if it was an ancient omen letting the people know that there was malice afoot. That there was no safety, no escape from the ill-intentions of others. The front was hundreds of kilometers from the city, however. Why on Earth should anyone be afraid? None of the residents, nor the military for that matter were sharp enough to pick up on mother nature's cries of fear.

Before long, it was midday. The morning fog had passed and the city was bustling with activity, as it usually is when the sun is shining above them. The day was set to be yet another unremarkable day in history, with residents and visitors alike moving within the cities streets, doing their day-to-day lives without any sort of fear–save for the war, of course.

As the sun started its descent back down beyond the horizon, a line of trucks dotting the highways made their way westwards into the city. They appeared to be yet another normal military convoy set to resupply on goods to be sent back out east, just another cog in the machine after all. As they entered the city that had instead spread themselves out amongst the city, placing themselves in strange locations. In front of schools, government buildings, military bases, and residential areas did these trucks find their destinations. Yet none thought to ask the drivers what they were doing. When the sunlight finally faded away until tomorrow, new bursts of orange glows littered across the city–and died out as quickly as they came.

After all was revealed, another soft fog had clouded itself inside the city–out of nowhere it seemed. It was as if this fog wasn't ordained by God Himself, but of man. A malicious one, at that.

options.name: Something's wrong.

title: ...And Bringeth The Taste of Metal
desc:
Within hours, the entire city of Konigsberg was dead. Desolate. From one end of the city to the other, not a single living, organic creature or plant was taking their required breaths. There was nothing but the soulless emptiness of silence. Not even God nor Mother Nature herself decided to make a sound either, as the thick, cloudy fog sat itself faintly upon the city.

Not before long, trucks kitted out with lead plating, and men cladded with hazmat suits and gas masks sped their way into the seemingly abandoned city. As the trucks approached the gates of the city, in droves of hundreds lie unmoving squirrels, birds, deer, cats, dogs, people–all of God's earthly creations lie as if they had all simultaneously met their maker.

When the men entered the city proper, they had finally met the most dreadful of sights. Men, women, children, all strewn about like a bunch of ragdolls had been dropped from the sky. Some died clutching their throats, some died holding on to their loved ones. Most died alone. All of them shared the same fate though: unimaginably painful radioactive burns.

And as the men began documenting the utter destruction of an ancient city, there was one–just one–question lingering in the thoughts of everyone there

options.name: What hath man wrought?

title: Nothingness Under the Earth
desc:
Artyom eyed wearily around, being a guard of these bunkers especially ones so close to the front was not an easy job. There were common events that would occur such as someone attempting to steal all the food, even though they clearly had enough. Artyom didn’t enjoy shooting people, especially Russians. He tried to think of these people as German agents but time and time again he would hesitate to take another human life even leading to him getting a demotion for his actions. Apparently he was not as tough as the average Black League soldier, and it showed. 

Sometimes while he stood outside the bunker he would wonder what would be happening inside of it, he saw many men coming in and out. Stocking food perhaps or maybe just putting finishing touches on it. Although slightly disillusioned with the way of things being run he still could find enjoyment  in his thoughts and of what could be down there. On one particular day the excitement of thought captured him and he decided to go inside. 

Following the workers to “check up on anything wrong” he was surprised to see how small it had looked, the propaganda had made the bunkers seem like labyrinths of concrete but this... This looked like it wouldn’t even hold a thousand people. “Would the Black League, would Yazov do this?” Artyom thought to himself. “No no clearly you just need to go further and there will be more” And so he went deeper and deeper into the facility. And yet it was all unfinished, he thought the war would break out in less than a month now and really there would be no way they would be able to finish this bunker. 

Leaving the bunker he exited and stood back at his post, the guard to the right of him responding 

“So how does it look? Good enough to watch the Germans waste away?”

He looked no younger than 17, Jesus were they conscripting that young. Artyom pondered before responding

options.name: “It’s just as good as the pictures.”

title: The Riot
desc:
War had been going on for God knows how long. And while the Russian news spoke of the Russian victories Artyom knew that deep down it was all pointless however cynical he was, all of that was brushed away as people started to flock towards some of the little public shelters. The one he was stationed at number A-1684 was one of the unlucky few, however if he just explained to the protestors that they all would have a chance in the bunker. If he could just tell the lie maybe some dumber part of himself will believe in what he was working for. 

That all came crashing down when a woman and her young child, maybe less than 10, appeared in the crowd, although it was disorganized and mainly full of those who were older. Aside from the few reluctant teenagers unwilling to join the army. 

“Please sir, my name is Alyona just take my child”

She picked up her child and amidst all the screaming and the shouting. Everything fell away, for once he had a choice in his life. He could either take the young boy and foster him as a new life. Or like everyone there he was to turn them both away, getting them to walk home once more back to their small little village which hadn’t changed much since Omsk’s control over it. 

However his time to decide ran out as reinforcements encircled the small throng of humanity. The commander of the garrison force had radioed for help from the local detachment near the front and soon enough. The firing soon began, like the Reunification Wars Russians were killing Russians once more. As the crowd dispersed quickly, he saw the young woman Alyona laying on the grass in a puddle of her own blood. Her son tugged at her and cried, as Artyom looked on. The kid was picked up and sent on his way back with the retreating crowd. 

“Fucking idiots they all are, why can’t they just trust the army” Blurted out from one of the advancing vanguard. “I mean we’re liberating Russia here and these liberals want to live in the bunkers? What a load of shit am I right?” the soldier responded to Artyom.

options.name: “Yeah... I guess it is.”

title: Finalé
desc:
It was Artyom’s day off, a simple but welcome pleasure to his life with the Black League. As he walked down the main street getting looks from the onlookers, among the soldiers they privately did not want to enter town after what was being called “The Red Afternoon”. After getting a newspaper from the stand and paying for it, he sat down. Opening the paper as he would any other day, his eyes looked at the front headline. In large and bold letters it exclaimed “Königsberg Has Been Captured” seeing this he knew the inevitable was close to occurring. Although he had been taught about this by his teachers in Basic Training he could not fathom that it had happened so quickly.

He knew his world was ending, although the people around him didn’t seem to notice. In due time the well astute citizens would spell it out for them. He got up out of his chair and began to run towards the bunker he once defended, in his full military uniform. Although he used it for a discount, maybe it could even save his life. Countless thoughts were rushing throughout his head, he thought back to seeing the bunker for the first time. Was the construction still going on, or maybe it was nothing at all. Perhaps Germany would for the good of the world accept it’s natural conclusion. With a simple peace and Russian hegemony, as idealistic as it was, it was better than accepting the end of humanity as a whole.

Nearing the bunker Artyom found that there was an eerie silence to it all. Besides for the industrial sounds emanating from the bunker itself. It was calming, relaxing even as the wind blew through his hair as he drew closer and closer to the entrance his heart sank deep into its chest. The door was drawn shut, attempting to reach anyone there he at first knocked on the cold metal only giving him echoes. Hearing the emergency sirens begin to blare on and on as a cacophony of noise began to displace the silence with pure fear and terror. As Artyom sat near the door he imagined back to the woman who went to give her child to him. He wondered what he was doing in all of this, “I just hope he’s safe” his mind told him. As the blinding light flashed before his eyes. One last thought crossed his mind

options.name: I just wish I could apologize to her.

title: Time was running thin on Oleg
desc:
His job was simple, plain and simple. Take the chemical weapons found in the Black Mountain and use them against the Germans. An easy task in concept alone, to launch such chemical attacks upon a nation the likes of which would rival The Great War localized in a single empire. It would be the first masterstroke of The Great Trial and one to rival the “Blitzkrieg” the Nazis used to attempt the conquering of Russia.

Staring at the map in mild disbelief he pondered what part or district of the city could be terrorized the most. Crossing his mind thoughts danced around his head of the Teutonic scum slowly choking on their own lungs slowly dissolving in their throats. The gas seeping through every corner of the streets and buildings. Creeping like a malignant ooze through masks and rags. 

Looking at the small instructional booklet given to him in code he soon deciphered the next few instructions. Finishing off the final touches Oleg masterfully plugged in code, taped in wires, and wound the watch on his hand so that eventually when the hands struck noon the device would go off. Packing the device away into his briefcase he set it aside on the floor next to his blanket barren cot, the springs rusted from age and coarse to the touch.

Sleeping on the cot in his rental for the month it was barren, spartan if one could call it. There were papers strewn about, propaganda from the League and ideological dog whistles and small wrappers of food. Parcels given to him by the League through postage. However the little the thin man ate he ate only what kept him healthy. Not indulging himself in the excesses as he saw the other German scum dine upon.

options.name: He slept soundly.

title: The Yellow City
desc:
Klara arose at roughly 5:30 AM, early for most but not for her. Going through the daily routine was simple: she’d eat some toast and jam with a small hint of butter, finish her planning for the day and set out in her Volkswagen on the daily commute. The breeze softly caressing her face as the windows roll down she sensed excitement in the air.

Arriving at the school she taught at, she parked her Bug in the respective parking zone and walked inside the heavy glass doors. Passing room by room she checked the watch, 7:13 AM was plastered on the clock as she went into her room.

Opening the door she saw once more how well her and her children decorated the room as it burst with personality. There were little drawings and past assignments posted stapled or drawn on the surrounding walls and the sun peaked ever so slightly through the half opened windows. Breathing in the fresh air she sat at her desk attentively.

Soon enough the children started petering in.

After the bell rang with an annoying clang the room fell silent. Addressing the class Klara spoke loud and concisely “Alright class let-” A large BANG rang out from the outside world the force of the explosion seemed to rock everyone to the core. Klara herself was thrown out of her chair and to the floor. After getting up she saw that at least all the children were under their desks. Hands over little heads, asides from the glass scraping the arm of one child relatively they were all ok.

In a shaky and shoddy tone Klara told the children it would be all ok and she would find out what was happening. Poking her head outside of the door the young woman eyed nervously around, the Russians surely have not invaded here and arrived this fast she thought to herself. As nervous thoughts danced around in her mind, she walked towards the once glass entrance doors, now shells of their former selves on the ground. The crunch of the glass as it stuck to her shoe sent pings of fear down her spine.

As she stared around her she saw a plume of smoke from the adjacent apartment building. However as she eyed the building another colored apparition floated through the air. A thickly yellow gas emitted from the hole in the building above. She immediately thought back to her father telling her of his experiences in the first world war. And what even was that awful stench she began to smell.

options.name: And then she began to cough.

title: A Weary Beast...
desc:
Timofey and Alexei were profoundly exhausted, having marched 10 miles just today, but there was no rest for the wicked. “New orders from high command,” Alexei’s radio crackled, both men leaning forward to listen intently. “There is a German position in the lowland ahead, Number 3 Platoon will proceed along the side of the road to support the motorized troops. Over”.

“I don’t believe it,” Timofey, the younger man, murmured miserably. “We've had no food or sleep in a day and a half! Constant German ambushes, counterattacks, snipers, and now they demand we just keep on marching like it’s nothing?! Just statistics to be drilled, dieted, treated like cattle, used as cannon fodder?” he ranted.

Alexei listened quietly before replying. “Accidents are common on the frontlines,” the older man advised. “If a hand, maybe a foot were to get injured, it wouldn't be questioned.” He kept his tone even, eyes locked with Timofey. “They can’t starve and deprive us for weeks without expecting a few accidents to happen, no?”

Timofey met his gaze. “And wounded soldiers need food and rest to get better, of course” he mused. “What’s the betting there’s going to be a lot of ‘accidents’ around here before long?”

“You said it yourself,” Alexei replied, “we’re not cattle and we won’t be driven across the steppe like a herd. Hell, a herd might be treated better. But unless something changes, we’re going to see a lot of men break, or worse.”

options.name: Hate leads to suffering.

title: ...And An Uncomfortable Reality
desc:
The door opened, and seemingly the air inside the room was sucked out. Evgeny barely heard the doorman call for him for his appointment. Appointment was a strong word, actually. It was a summons. 
He stood up, attempting to suppress his nausea. He took one step forward, and another, until he walked in stride. Whatever his fate, he would not meet it with cowardice. Each door opened as if a portal to another world, each increasing in relative opulence to the next and the consecutive hallways almost seemed to expand in radiance and size. It all led to a throne room of sorts. Yazov had insisted his office be at the epicenter of the building. It was more bunker than  workspace, the result of his own paranoia. Pitranov witnessed Yazov pacing wolf-like next to a truly gigantic fireplace. It cast a shadow large enough to loom over the entire room. He swallowed hard. 
"Comrade Marshal. I have the report you requested of me regarding the economic state of the League and the lack of offensive progress." He stuffed his hands behind his back, praying the decorum would save him. Yazov continued his pacing, merely signalling for him to continue. "I'm afraid I have pinned the reason for our great stall. A state of exhaustion has taken over the economy. Circulation of money is almost nil. The people have hoarded their remaining material wealth. Our policies of austerity have taken a larger and earlier toll than normal. I fear if we do nothing and continue mass-spending on the Army, then..." 
Pitranov's lip quivered uncontrollably as he finally saw Yazov face him. His face was lined with exhaustion, darker even than the shadow that appeared at his back. With bloodshot eyes, he made another quick hand gesture, and the blast-door Pitranov came through locked shut.

options.name: And whose fault is that?

title: The Wells Run Dry
desc:
Petronov flipped through the binders and binders of names, graphs, and figures collated at his recruitment station in one of Samara's countless pre-built housing districts. It had been a quiet day, an abnormality for sure, one he lit a cigarette to calm the impending chiding from his superiors at the next Sub-District Recruitment Officer Summit a fortnight from now. However, as he continued flipping through the figures, a trend began to emerge, and suddenly, the issue seemed much more deserving of another cigarette.

Recruitment was down, and unlike other periods, it was no longer a blip. Figure after figure, graph after graph showed the indelible downward curve, an ever-decreasing slope that varied only in how many fewer recruits walked through his door to give their lives to the Black League. From a peak of more than 2,000 fresh and young recruits entering his center in one day, now numbers were lucky to dip into the hundreds per week. Petronov's hands and lip began to quiver, his eyes darting from side to side and forehead collecting sweat. He rushed for the phone, calling a colleague in the city. He normally would not give that smug bastard the pleasure of seeing his weakness, but he had to know.

Dmitri's voice was hoarse as ever even through the static of the phone line. After exchanging thinly veiled pleasantries, he got to the point.

"Dmitri. What is happening to recruitment? My station has hardly seen anyone enlist. Is it the same with you?" There was a silence on the other line before Dmitri cautiously responded.

"You're having the same problem?"

options.name: "By all accounts, we've emptied out everyone here."

title: The Engine Sputters
desc:
There is a fundamental cowardice with the clerk. Whether he works in the deepest bowels of Army Intelligence, or an office far behind the lines, it is that fundamental cowardice that remains a constant factor. It is a deep-rooted aversion to presenting failure. At least in the Black League, that fear made sense. An excess of failure carried a sentence. Nevertheless, it seeps through and corrodes government and institutions further than any Germanic intelligence network or purposeful campaign of sabotage.

It is a disease that manifests when a clerk in the Finance Ministry incorporates a surplus into the new year's budget. It is a disease that manifests when an Intelligence Officer does not have the will to report new enemy formations that should not exist. It is the cowardice of a propaganda officer who can not admit that his efforts produce fewer and fewer recruits every day. They collect like water pressing against a dam, steadily applying more pressure to the failing stones that make it, each drop seeping through the ailing concrete and threatening to burst out the other end.

Steadily, as a foreign diplomat fails to report that foreign commitments grow scarcer and scarcer, and bureaucrats within the Ministry of Health report that their hospitals still have the capacity, even as they discard those too costly to save, the dam that holds the war effort threatens to break asunder. Now, as German armies recuperate from the relentless offensive and begin to advance, the dam stands vulnerable and at its precipice. All it would take is one well-timed strike to bring the whole rotten structure down.

options.name: A rot that extends further than any mold.

title: The Engine Stops
desc:
The patrol on horseback saw smoke on the horizon kilometers before they encountered the convoy. Packing the road and the surrounding fields were churned-up scraps of metal, some of which still burned and warped from the intense heat of battle that took place. The remnants of rifles, foodstuffs, spare parts, and other assorted military goods joined them, almost all of it burnt or otherwise destroyed beyond use. The grass was charred black, and the torn apart bodies, or at least what could be identified as bodies, littered it.

Maksim simply plugged his nose and signaled for his men to dismount and move toward the ruined trucks. They had just been rotated off the line, not that it came with any benefit. The Luftwaffe was perfectly capable of hitting anyone, or anything, it wanted, no matter how far behind the line they hid. His stomach rumbled, and he hunched over in pain. Rotation also didn't mean improved rations. Command claimed they were needed for the men who "actually fought". He signaled for his men to quicken the pace and headed over to one of the destroyed trucks. This expedition wasn't sanctioned by command, but given the lack of presumed survivors, nobody would know any better.

In its flatbed was nothing much of value. Ruined ammunition and pieces of flesh were strewn across the splintered wood and tattered canvas tarp. The next series of trucks didn't yield anything better. Suddenly, one of his men shouted out. Maksim raced towards him. His sergeant held aloft a crate full of raw potatoes looted from one of the burnt-out trucks. Maksim quickly ordered it tied to the back of one of the horses. They would eat well tonight, not that it would last longer. As he walked back to his horse, he spotted what appeared to be a survivor amongst the wreckage, a trooper no older than 18. His face was charred almost beyond recognition, hair burnt to the skin. He reached out weakly, croaking for something. His voice sounded like he was speaking through a torn paper bag.

options.name: Maksim ignored him. They had gotten what they came for.

title: A True Believer
desc:
Piotyr leapt aside as the concrete mixer tipped, filling the hole that he had dug in the frozen earth: a foundation for yet another bunker. For the past eight weeks, he had been here, in some remote part of the Urals, building bunkers to protect his people from the coming storm. The cold conditions and small rations would have made almost anyone complain, if not desert outright, but not Piotyr. Piotyr had faith. Faith that they would destroy the Teutonic menace. Faith in Russia. Faith in Yazov. This faith had driven him to work at a furious pace, and along with a handful of other true believers in his construction crew, his crew had built bunker after bunker, faster than any cadre crew in this place, far far away from any civilization or anything to really speak of.

So far their efforts had gone unnoticed by the government, not that Piotyr cared. Piotyr’s family had been killed by the Teutons, not in one swoop– that would have been a mercy– but one after the other. His parents that he barely remembered had died in Barbarossa, executed by one of the Einsatzgruppen. His brother– the brother that saved him from the fate of his parents– had died a soldier in the West Russian War. His wife and children had died in one of the Luftwaffe’s accursed bombing raids while they had been living in Vyatka. After this decades-long torture at the hands of the Teuton, Piotyr only had one goal, one driving force as he layered brick after brick, hole after frozen hole:

Revenge...

options.name: ... no matter the cost.

title: Diamonds in the Rough
desc:
“Aysen shoveled through the frostbitten, packed dirt with as much grit and determination as he could muster. Echoes of gunshots, just beyond the distance, reminded him of the consequences if he failed to do so. Every brief moment of rest between shovels was cut short as he plunged his equipment back into the Earth, just to drown out the sounds around him.

Ever since that bastard Yazov and his soldiers, draped in black, had marched into his homeland, he and his fellow Yakuts knew nothing but the back breaking labor of the mines. What was once peaceful co-existence, albeit tense at times, with those he once called his countrymen soon became a violent subjugation as any in Yakutia able to work were forced at gunpoint into contributing to 'the reclamation of Russia'.

"No cost too great, and no sacrifice too small," they would repeat to the workers, day after day, as they did nothing but sit back and watch their endless toiling.

Once, there was a time Aysen would've protested the actions of the Black League, perhaps even rebel if he had the strength of his youth. Now those thoughts were now brushed aside, replaced with the memories of his fellow Yakut, his own friends and family, being beaten and bloodied by the guards of the labor site. Even children, already being indoctrinated into the hate of the Black League, would kick at worker's knees as they passed, "not adequately pursuing their patriotic duty," as their instructors would say.

And so Aysen continued to shovel, through monotony, through heavy snow storms, through bright skies, through brutal winters, and warm summers. Perhaps, he thought, all his hard work would be worth something one day.”

options.name: How many shifts are there in an eternity?

title: An Unmeasurable Anger
desc:
An emergency cabinet meeting had been called by Yazov, who had grown frustrated with the news that the war situation was not necessarily developing to Russia’s advantage. This could not continue, and someone had better have an explanation. Everyone took their seats, the room deathly quiet. “Gentlemen” Yazov finally said “the line is stagnant, the advance halted. Resources seem to be falling into a black hole” he leaned forward, fixing the cabinet with a chilling gaze. “And I want to know why”.

Those present looked nervously around, one man tugged anxiously at his collar while another fidgeted and flicked his eyes to the others, hoping someone else would speak first.
