The one true god was mankind.

options.name: And mankind is long since dead.

title: RAD_NA.43.t
desc:
Finally, it was happening. After years of signs and shouting and little listening, what Keith had predicted was now coming to pass. Six of the Seven Seals had been opened, and now, as the Seventh would soon descend upon the Earth, Keith could witness the power and the glory, and embrace his Lord. The air raid sirens blared, so loud that the entire City of Angels could hear. He stared up into the sky, expectant, anxious, ready.

As he was staring he could discern, far away above the clouds, a black dot, trailing fire through the sky. It was happening; Judgement Day had come. Soon, Keith would find himself in the arms of the Lord, his God, and he leapt with joy. Unable to control himself, he began to run towards the streaking object. As terrified onlookers ran and screamed for their lives, Keith sprinted towards his perceived salvation.

Suddenly, an immense, awesome flash of flaring light overcame Keith's vision, and he was blinded. He did not care, for none who see the face of God shall live. Standing blindly in place, arms outstretched, he recited the verse to all who may hear it, "And the angel took the censer, and filled it with fire of the altar, and cast it into the earth: and there were voices, and thunderings, and lightnings, and an earthquake. And the seven angels which had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound. And I heard a great voice out of the temple saying to the seven angels, Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth."

And so the vials were poured, and Keith was no more.

options.name: Who shall be able to stand?

title: RAD_NA.41.t

options.name: ...and still there was one.

title: RAD_NA.33.t
desc:
Time passes, and the world moves on from the Great Tragedy. New civilizations rise and fall from the corpses of old. Children grow into adulthood into elderhood before they depart to the Reverse Side. In twenty-year stretches, more of the past is reclaimed, unearthed, and eventually reused.

It began when a city in Turtleland rediscovered the speakpole: a nifty little piece of Old World technology that, so the Reclaimers said, uses vibrations in the air to send messages to another piece of Old World technology called the speakbox. Convenient for communicating with other people from distances away, they were envisioned.

Then the Reclaimers found an unusually well-preserved collection of "speakards" in Excavation Site MO-12. Pictures of well-dressed young men and women line their clearhard surfaces, with names like "Bob Dylan" and "The Beach Boys" hanging above their heads. Someone noticed that, placed carefully onto a speakbox's carrying slot, the speakards fit perfectly well.

Many times in human history had accidents resulted in monumental changes that altered its course. In this case, what happened was nothing less than a flowering of songs from mankind's better times in the present. Through this accident an integral piece of mankind's collective culture, once forgotten, now finds new life in an age of wonder and hope.

options.name: California dreamin', on such a winter's day...

title: RAD_NA.20.t
desc:
As the sun set below the horizon, a man offloaded the final can of fuel into the thirsty tank of a generator. With several aggressive pulls of a cord, the generator roared to life, emitting a steady whir. Not far off, a set of lights flickered to life, brightly illuminating a grassy yard upon which an intimate gathering of men and women sat beneath the light, alcoholic drinks in hand.

As the power brought the yard to life much like the daytime sun, a music player was hauled over to the gathering and in turn connected to an electrical outlet. As electricity was fed to the device, loud, upbeat tunes began to emerge from its speakers. The group reveled in the euphoria of the music, and the memories it brought. Memories of a world seemingly without woes. Memories of an easier time. For one last moment, the hardships of the world could be forgotten, as they faded away like the passing of a dream.

The group erupted in laughter as jovial stories from a world now lost were shared. They continued to down their beverages with unusual speed, enjoying the few they had remaining. There were little more to go around.

The tune on the music player changed, and a woman of the group greeted the song with a dance. With several of the group singing along with the familiar lyrics, the others joined in on the dance. Laughter sounded off once again as the short moment seemed to extend into an eternity.

The night dragged on as the sky glowed with the unobstructed shine of the distant stars. Empty bottles lay scattered upon the ground as the group sat now in silent conversation, reveling in the final moments of the old world. The lights suddenly dimmed, and came back to full brightness again near immediately after, as the music player grew quiet for a brief moment in tandem. The generator audibly sputtered and choked upon the other side of the yard, as the group were once again met with their reality, like vivid memories of a forgotten nightmare. As the generator offered its final cough, the lights flickered into indefinite darkness. Finally, seconds later, the music offered its final notes, and the group sat under the silent starlight once again.

options.name: All things must end.

title: RAD_NA.15.t
desc:
The child screamed into life at 11:57PM, weighing a good 7.6 pounds, sporting a small mane of blonde hair and two brown eyes. His mother held him adoringly, his father looked on with a smile. They hadn't named him yet; it was hard to name something so beautiful and wonderful and important. The radio in the hospital room played, smooth quiet jazz - it was all perfect. The beginnings of a family.

Then perfection came crashing down. The smooth jazz, in a heartbeat, cut to static - then a buzz.

"ATTENTION," it blared in a monotone voice, "ATTENTION. This is the Emergency Broadcast System. Take shelter immediately. Take shelter immediately. This is not a drill.

Repeat: This is not a drill. An enemy attack is being launched against the United States. Take shelter immediately and stay tuned to this frequency for further instructions."

The nameless child woke and began to sob, sooned joined by his mother. The man's heart leapt into his throat. Not now. Why did it have to be now? He slumped into his seat, cradling his head in his hands for a moment. He knew she couldn't move, and he knew he would never leave either of them here.

The mother whispered quiet assurances to her son with no name as the father slid into the bed, wrapping his arms around his wife and son, tears streaming down his face.

The child cooed and giggled at his parents' faces, and as his hand curled around his mother's pinky, a blinding flash set the world ablaze.

Years later, scavengers would find the silhouettes of a man, a woman, and a child in the ruins of a hospital.

options.name: All this for lines on a map.

title: RAD_NA.8.t
desc:
Father Jacobs sat in his old white rocking chair, a contented smile across his face. Today had been a good day, and for that he praised the Lord. He watched from the top of the hill his church sat upon, down at the lights of the city far, far away. It was so peaceful on these nights, enough for him to forget the constant fear and anxiety that permeated every facet of the last few months. There was no worry about war tonight, only the comforts of freedom and the comforts of the Lord.

He didn't see the bombers, but he heard them. He thought they must have been from the airport at first--but planes never flew over his hill. Then he thought it was a military exercise. They did seem to be on the highest alert lately. Maybe it was...

The flash cut him off.

He flung his hands in front of his eyes and fell backwards out of his chair, lying in the dirt for a moment, blinking fitfully in a futile attempt to clear the blinding white haze that obscured his vision. He wanted so badly to simply lie there forever, to not look upon what awaited him, but he knew that he had to do it. He wearily brought himself to his feet, quaking fearfully, and waited until his eyesight had cleared. What he saw before him caused his heart to drop to his stomach.

The cloud was the first thing he noticed. They hadn't been lying when they said it was like a mushroom. It was exactly like one, really, but made of fire, dreadful fire, and a thick black smoke that could blot out the sun. He looked down, and all that was before him was rubble and fire.

This was hell, he realized then. It had to be hell. How could a God be good and allow this? He sank to his knees as he watched, thinking of the families he attended. He thought of the children--how terrified they must have been, in their final moments, before they were consumed by that damned fire.

The ground quaked beneath him as the smoke rushed towards him from the horizon, but he didn't care. The nightmare would be over soon.

As hellfire washed over Father Jacobs, he cursed God for letting his children die so cruelly.

options.name: Faith cannot escape the flames of Hell.

title: RAD_NA.2.t
desc:
In a great bunker named simply D1, many hid in fear as the world above them was torn to the ground. The people of D1 would live for years, and years, before slowly they began to leave.

Disagreements and arguments caused the first ten to go, ten of the original group, and they were followed by twenty, and more and more of D1's people began to drift away. Years would pass, before the final remaining survivors of D1, and their children, would leave the bunker. Their children named themselves for the city that D1 sat under, Cheyenne, and would form a tribe, traveling across the plains of what was once America, once more learning to train and ride the horses that rode free, and hunt the Buffalo and other native animals.

They would, many years from then, come into conflict with other tribes, from outside the Plains, or descended from D1. Across America the Cheyenne would travel, forming federations, warring with other tribes, hunting for their food, and exploring what people claim was once a civilization. To them, it was simply another passing reminder that where they rode, their people had, in one way or another, for generations.

options.name: Across America, the Natives roam.

title: Summary of the Deindustrialization Action in Helsinki
desc:
1. Dispatch a certain scale of armed personnel to factories in the Helsinki region, such as **Outokumpu Steelworks**, **Wärtsilä Marine Power**, **Kemira Chemical Group**, and **Patria Aviation Factory**, to maintain order and prevent sabotage.
2. Establish a Special Interrogation Team to question factory management personnel to obtain statistics on personnel and equipment, inventory machinery and means of production suitable for rail transport, and classify and grade Finnish technical personnel.
3. Alliance industrial backbone personnel and Finnish technical personnel are responsible for dismantling machinery and equipment, while Finnish prisoners of war are used to transport containers and heavy equipment.
4. Control and manage the families of Finnish technical personnel, and execute uncontrollable individuals.
5. Commandeer the local railway system; dismantled equipment and materials are to be transferred from Helsinki to Arkhangelsk, and subsequently moved to industrial bases east of the Ural Mountains.
6. Provide appropriate resettlement for Finnish technical personnel, including setting up barracks and distributing food.
7. Following the operation's conclusion, sapper teams are to carry out total **mechanical destruction, explosive demolition, and chemical contamination** of any equipment and material that could not be moved.

options.name: —Approved.

title: The Double-Headed Eagle on the Snow
desc:
This year, winter came exceptionally early and cold to Finland. Emil Koivunen stepped on knee-deep snow, his axe striking the frozen spruce trunk with a dull *thud*. His breath condensed into white frost on his eyebrows, and every inhale felt like swallowing ice shards. He looked up at the grey sky; Finland's sky was usually clear, but now it was veiled in an ominous, grey haze.

Suddenly, a piercing siren tore through the air. Emil knew something was wrong and sprinted home, then hurried with his wife, Liisa, and children into the cellar. Outside, there was no expected roar of explosions, only a deathly silence, and a chilling *hiss* like a venomous snake spreading over the land. Closely following, a strange, subtly yellowish-green mist crept silently and swiftly along the snow's surface from the edge of the forest, engulfing everything. Clearly, this was man-made poison gas! Emil peered cautiously through the cellar door crack, seeing his neighbor, old Jonas, stumble out of his house, only to fall heavily into the snow after a few steps like a piece of dead wood, his body violently convulsing. Emil faintly heard a terrifying gurgling sound from his throat, like a drowning man. The old man's skin quickly erupted in hideous blisters, and he soon stopped moving.

An unknown time passed, and silence reigned. The air in the cellar was suffocatingly foul. Emil carefully pushed the door open slightly. Outside was terrifyingly quiet, only the wind moaning. Stiff corpses were scattered on the snow, their postures twisted in agony.

The sound of heavy leather boots crunching the snow grew nearer. There were three men, all wearing unfamiliar dark grey greatcoats, but the striking **golden double-headed eagle** insignia on their armbands declared their identity. The leader's vulture-like eyes fixed on Emil's gaze. Unfortunately, a soldier discovered the cellar entrance. He pulled out a strange-looking instrument, operated it twice, and seemingly detected people underground. The soldier gestured, and several dark gun muzzles were instantly pointed at them.

"Out! Finnish pig!" the soldier motioned for Emil to come out. Emil, his wife, and children trembled as they crawled out of the cellar and stood on the cold snow. The soldiers were expressionless, looking at them like livestock waiting for slaughter. One of them, whose gaze fell upon Liisa's pale but still beautiful face, let slip a chilling, cruel sneer. He unhooked the canteen from his waist, unscrewed the cap, and poured a little of the liquid onto the snow. Instantly, a pungent chemical odor wafted up. He squatted down and, using his gloved hand, scooped up a handful of filthy, chemically-tainted melted snow and **brutally smeared it onto Liisa's face**.

Liisa let out a short scream; her skin instantly burned and turned red. The soldier studied her pain, watching Emil's face contort with fury and despair, a muffled, satisfied laugh rumbling in his throat. Emil's eyes were bloodshot; he tried to lunge but was stopped by another cold rifle barrel pressing against his forehead. After what seemed like an age, Liisa gradually lost life. Apparently satisfied with their expressions of despair, the man waved his hand.

options.name: Then, 'Bang, bang, bang, bang—'

title: Vengeance Thirty Years Later
desc:
Lakes. The forests and lakes of Karelia had never been this lively in thirty years. It was here, once upon a time, that Finnish traitors, along with Teutonic planes and tanks, began the invasion. Thirty years have passed—enough time for a generation to grow from innocent children to rifle-carrying soldiers.

After the battle, black-clad soldiers escorted a column of young Finnish prisoners of war. They marched in three ranks, heads bowed, over muddy, icy ground, their feet worn with blood blisters, their clothes soaked through by the cold rain. If someone couldn't walk, the black-clad soldiers pulled him from the line and **executed him on the spot**, leaving the corpse behind.

They passed through deserted villages, glimpsing houses with walls covered in curses written in Russian, like a tourist's "So-and-so was here." Underneath the walls were piles of corpses, some burned, throats slit, or torn apart by bullets. Several others, men and women, old and young, lay naked and piled together, with purplish faces and grotesque smiles, like a heap of long-uncleaned garbage.

After an unknown number of days, they arrived at a **temporary internment camp** surrounded by barbed wire. Here, the officers of the black-clad soldiers inspected each prisoner: only those who could **remain standing after a severe punch** were kept. They would later be transported by train to Onega and then to military factories in the rear.

"Drown the rest of these in the lake. Next batch."

options.name: The sons shall pay for the fathers' debts.

title: Good Man or Bad Man?
desc:
Grisha's rough, warm fingers tightly gripped the cold Mosin-Nagant rifle stock. Around him, the roar of the crowd surged in waves: "Let the Teutonic pigs pay their blood debt!", and Grisha's chest heaved with emotion—look, this was the strength of the Slavic nation! He felt the whip marks left by the German foreman when he was still a slave, faintly burning beneath his ribs, and blood rushed to his head; he was even a little dizzy with excitement. The **Black League** had brought the "**Great Trial**"; they had shattered the shackles of the so-called "New Order" and brought freedom, reeking of blood!

Several people in old German-style clothes were shoved out, their faces ashen. Grisha's gaze locked onto one old man—**Von Erich**, a German language teacher before the war. When Grisha was ten, he had been struck on the palm with a ruler by him for mispronouncing an "R." The memory of humiliation instantly ignited the flame in Grisha's eyes. It was him! These high and mighty "master race" people—who were they to insult him like this?!

An officer wearing the double-headed eagle armband roared from the wooden platform, enumerating the Germans' sins: "For Mother Russia! Execute the judgment!" Grisha's column was pushed forward. Mechanically, he raised his rifle, and the cold sight framed Von Erich's panicked face. The old man's cloudy eyes seemed to recognize him, flashing a hint of surprise, his lips moving silently. Grisha's finger rested on the trigger; he wanted to scrutinize this arrogant face...

"**Aim!**" the command thundered. But Grisha's breathing suddenly stopped. The face in the sight overlapped with a fragment of memory: this was not the ferocious face of the foreman, nor the cold, cruel face of the SS, but just the **desperate, terrified face of an old man** in an ill-fitting old suit, trembling with fear—this old man had also once frowned and tossed him an aspirin when he had a high fever. Although the old man's face always carried an expression of disgust when facing him, as if giving charity... he also remembered one time when he was beaten raw by a Wehrmacht officer, and the old man had tossed him a bottle of antiseptic. The memories instantly extinguished his boiling fervor.

"**Fire!**"

"*Bang—*"

Grisha stood still. In a daze, the old man had already fallen into a pool of blood. His rifle-holding hand was trembling uncontrollably. All around were the celebrating crowds and the shouts of "**Long live the Great Trial!**" He opened his mouth, but his throat felt blocked. His gaze moved past the crowd, landing on the corpse at the foot of an oak tree. A worn German pamphlet slipped out of the old man's pocket, falling into the blood. The stained pages were blown open by the wind, revealing lines of unfamiliar poetry—Goethe's *Faust*. A small doubt emerged in the bottom of Grisha's heart, which had just been filled with vengeful fanaticism: "**What if some Germans weren't that bad?**"

options.name: But he only dared bury this doubt deep in his heart.

title: Vengeance for Vengeance
desc:
"I curse their mother! How did these Slav bastards get here again?!" Inside a command post in **Moskowien**, a general roared into the phone. "You better prepare immediately to deal with these Slavic vermin! Oh, by the way, I'll ask the higher-ups to send you some more troops. You absolutely must catch those disobedient slaves in the factory and make an example of them, or we're finished! Did you understand?!"

Having said this, the general threw the phone and collapsed weakly into his seat, the **West Russian War** from over twenty years ago flashing before his eyes—that war almost crushed the vital colonial territory of Moskowien. Fortunately, the Aryan race was favored by heaven, preventing those Slavic beasts from winning. He was sure this time would be the same.

Thinking this, the general's tension slightly eased. He went to the mirror to adjust his uniform, put on his cap, and checked if anything was dirty or torn. He wouldn't want to command his soldiers with a messy face.

Just then, a loud explosion came from outside the window, startling the general, who staggered and fell to the floor. "What's going on?! Have those Slavs already attacked?" He stood up and looked out the window: yellowish-green gas permeated everywhere, and large and small corpses of soldiers lay on the ground. As a military man, he suddenly realized this was a **poison gas shell** or something similar. A wave of panic surged through his heart; he needed to hurry and inform others that those beasts had used **chemical weapons**, but it was too late. A shell was flying straight towards his location, and just as he picked up the phone, the shell hit.

"A beautiful shot! Kosov, I heard that Teutonic bastard in that house was an old general. Now they'll know what pain is! Hahahaha!" Kosov ignored him. He just kept aiming to himself. He could see how terrified those scattering Germans were, and he had seen the same fear—on the faces of his **wife and five-year-old daughter**. He could still recall the scene when his wife and daughter were executed by the Nazis. He had just escaped from a slave labor factory and saw two females, one big and one small, publicly shot by the Nazis. He pitied them then. But when he had a chance to look closer, he swore he would make these Nazi pigs taste what it was like to be tortured and killed. After escaping to the fragmented Russian lands, he was quickly drawn to the **Black League**'s ideology and became an excellent warrior.

He fired another shell, and a large mess of blood and rotten flesh flew into the air, but Kosov felt no fear. On the contrary, he felt a hint of... **pleasure**?

options.name: Serves them right.

title: Redemption or Death
desc: "I heard you captured a batch of German soldiers?" "Yes, and we're planning to give them a good welcome." Inside a barracks, two Black League officers were talking. Not far from them, in a relatively hidden room, a group of people were trying every means to extract useful information from the prisoners, but despite clubs, electric shocks, and **ripping out fingernails**, the German POWs refused to disclose even a tiny bit of their unit's movements. "You really have guts, don't you? Fine, let me see how much guts you really have!" the leading Black League soldier shouted at the prisoners. "Someone! Take these dog-fucking Teutonic bastards to the wall. I'm not going to baby them anymore!" A group of tall men dragged and pulled the German soldiers to a dilapidated wall. Anger still burned in the eyes of the German soldiers; they seemed deeply unwilling. "Line them up! I have something to say to them!" Though troublesome, these 'gutsy' Teutons were persuaded to line up. "Do you know why I brought you here?" "Go fuck your mother, you Slavic bastard! I don't care to listen to your—" A gunshot interrupted the German soldier's roar, and he fell to the ground, lifeless. "You Teutons are truly ill-mannered savages. The name 'Germanic barbarians' is entirely accurate, wouldn't you agree?" The remaining German soldiers, seeing the increasingly cold corpse of their comrade, had much of the fire in their eyes extinguished. They mostly said nothing, just staring blankly around. "Alright... listen! Bastards! You might remember what your ancestors or you yourselves did during the war! I'm not referring to one specific war, but every single one! We know all about your cruel abuse of our compatriots! You Nazi pigs are the absolute lowest of humanity! And yet you call yourselves the noble Aryan race—nothing but a self-deceiving lie! I bet you don't even understand your Führer, just blindly worship him! Let me tell you, your so-called great Führer is nothing but a junkie who spends his days doing drugs, engaging in debauchery, and doesn't care whether you live or die! He only mindlessly sends you into battle! But he won't give you any benefit after the fight!" After a moment of silence, seeing no reaction from the prisoners, the Black League soldier continued: "I don't know if you're regretting or cursing, but it doesn't matter! I'll give you two choices! The first: join our **great vengeance undertaking** and atone for your sins. The second: perhaps it will make you seem 'gutsy,' which is to refuse to follow our orders! If you choose the second... Good! Now, those who want to join the **Redemption Brigade** and become glorious members, raise your hand!" A dead silence followed. The German soldiers exchanged glances, constantly wavering and deciding in their hearts. Finally, **two** German soldiers raised their hands.

options.name: “Take the rest to the gas chamber; let them have a good time.”

title: Inside the Factory
desc:
Just like any other day, Ilich was working around the clock in a **meat factory** in **German-controlled Moskowien**. He had forgotten how long he had been here—days? months? even years? He was now like an emotionless machine, processing parts on the assembly line every day. Seeing one compatriot after another collapse from overwork around him, he dared not imagine their fate—would they be saved, or simply thrown out to feed the rats? He didn't know.

But this Ilich was a disguise for the Germans. Months ago, he had secretly contacted a **partisan group** and helped them hide weapons. He and the partisans had been waiting for the right moment.

Finally, his chance came. When news arrived that Russia was united again and attacking Germany, he would never forget the look of terror on the faces of the factory guards. He watched their horrified expressions, struggling to suppress a sneer, and picked up a **wrench** nearby... "Striking the back of a person's head with full force can be instantly fatal," he recalled the lesson the partisan taught him. He implemented this test behind the guard, who hadn't noticed his approach.

The great test succeeded. He searched the fallen guard, finding a pistol and bullets. He shouted: "**Compatriots! Answer the call of our great Motherland! Stand up! Straighten your spines!**" Dozens of other workers responded, and together they killed the remaining few guards in the factory. Ilich immediately ran to their usual meeting spot to link up with the partisans, but the person who greeted him was a stranger wearing a **black uniform** and a **gas mask**. The man handed him a gas mask, introducing himself as a soldier of the "**Black League**," now engaged in the great vengeance undertaking against the Teutons. Ilich immediately understood what he meant and led the Black League soldier to the warehouse where he usually stored weapons.

options.name: “Distribute these rifles later. Your time has come.”

title: An Ordinary Day
desc:
"How many days have I been here?" Hans mused to himself. Many months ago, he was taken in by the Black League as a German prisoner of war into a unit seemingly called the **Redemption Brigade**. In this unit, he was not treated as a regular soldier; instead, he seemed more like an object to be used and discarded.

And that was indeed the truth. One afternoon, Hans's company was required to assist a Black League regular army unit in a combat mission, and the task assigned to him was... "Fucking **human mine detector**? Is the person who gave this order an idiot?" Hans cursed fiercely in his heart when he heard his mission.

"I can see that some of you might have opinions! Don't forget! This is what you deserve! We will never forget the cruelty you Teutons inflicted upon our Slavic compatriots! If any of you dare to disobey orders, we will throw you directly onto a landmine!" The captain of the Redemption Brigade shouted at them. Hans glared at him fiercely, thankful the captain didn't see it.

....

Hans and his group were taken to a marked area. A wooden sign was haphazardly inscribed with: "**Minefield**." Hans wanted to open his mouth and say something but felt a rifle barrel pressed against his back. He immediately swallowed the words he was about to say and cautiously stepped forward, detecting.

About ten minutes later, Hans was still alive. He lamented how good his luck was. But just then, he suddenly felt an abnormal looseness in the soil. He immediately realized he might have stepped on a landmine.

"**Am I going to die?**" Hans suddenly thought, but he wasn't willing to die just like that. A dangerous idea popped into his mind. He located the nearest Black League soldier, waved his hand to him, and tried to call him over. The Black League soldier seemed unsuspicious and walked toward him step by step.

"Yes, just like that..." Hans murmured softly. He estimated the killing range of the landmine beneath his foot, doing his best to draw the man closer without attracting attention.

Just as he was about to succeed, a gunshot rang out. Hans instantly felt his body go limp and he fell down.

With a loud explosion, Hans dissolved into a **cloud of blood mist**.

options.name: The little Teutonic bastard was quite cunning.

title: Oh, How Pure
desc:
"A bright, sunny day, isn't it?" Belikov said to a half-dead German soldier on the ground.

"Honestly, Teuton, if I were you, I'd have asked the great Führer to give me a gas mask, but he has to spend the money for your gas masks on **Pervitin**, right?" The German soldier said nothing; he was close to losing consciousness.

Belikov kicked the soldier hard. The soldier seemed startled, violently flinching and staring at Belikov with panic-stricken eyes.

"Teutonic bastard, do you know how the Nazis dealt with our great Slavs, huh?" Belikov raised his rifle, aimed at the German soldier's knee, and pulled the trigger.

"Fuck! Please, I beg you, let me go!" The German soldier screamed in pain. "Haha! Teuton! So you feel pain too!" Belikov slammed the rifle butt into the German soldier's abdomen, then dragged his body and threw it onto the street. A hissing sound of gas release emerged, and **yellowish-green gas** instantly permeated the street. Norton, the tortured German soldier, could only watch helplessly as his former comrades fell to the ground in panic. He, too, gradually lost the strength to control himself, and his vision blurred. "Mama..." he whispered with his last ounce of strength.

Belikov looked through the lenses of his gas mask at the Teutonic bastards gradually collapsing on the ground, the smile at the corner of his mouth becoming unstoppable. He used his rifle to deliver the final judgment on those German soldiers who still had a breath left.

"Oh, Teuton, you should thank me for ending your suffering..." Belikov murmured, pulling the trigger to execute a German soldier who was tearfully crawling forward.

As the yellowish-green gas filled the street, Belikov returned to his squad.

options.name: “Mission complete, Comrade Commander.”

title: Chemical Warfare
desc:
One morning, Müller woke up. He rubbed his eyes, pushed open the door, and went to the ranch. He skillfully poured water and fed his livestock. After finishing all this, he returned home to prepare breakfast. While preparing breakfast, Müller looked out the window and noticed something unusual: some animals seemed to have fallen down. Unsure if he had seen correctly, he rubbed his eyes and looked again.

"Fuck," Müller whispered, then opened the door and rushed out. He watched as one animal after another collapsed before his eyes. Disbelieving, he rushed to the fallen animals, wanting to check if they had been hurt. Just then, he seemed to smell a very unpleasant odor. He looked up, glancing around, and observed a stranger in a **black uniform** and a **gas mask** not far away, writing something with a pen and paper. He wanted to confront the man about what he had done, but found he couldn't exert any strength. He was now lying helplessly on the ground, looking at his livestock, his life's work, but powerless to do anything.

"**The effect is excellent, Comrade Commander. That Teutonic farmer and his livestock were almost instantly knocked out upon smelling the poison gas, but I think we can strengthen the gas. That way, those Teutonic bastards might die faster. Report complete.**"

"Received. Inform all units. **Mass deployment of poison gas shells is approved.**"

options.name: Let those Teutonic devils see our power!

title: Biological Warfare
desc:
"Today wasn't much different from usual, except I was called out by the commander to look for nearby drinkable water sources. That sounds a lot like ancient warfare, doesn't it!

But the reality seems much crueler. Ever since my comrades drank the water I brought, they've been continuously getting sick. Some lucky ones survive, but they're basically no different from the dead. Some aren't so lucky. I hope this is just my illusion.

My commander called me over. He asked me where I got the water, and he was very angry. I was terrified, so I could only tell him the truth."

Albert stopped writing and followed his commander and a small group of people to the small ditch where he fetched the water. They took back some samples and handed them to the research team, anxiously waiting for the test results.

"I seem to have messed up. More and more people are dying. We just gave the water to the research team to investigate. I hope this is just my illusion."

But reality delivered a heavy blow. The report from the research team said they detected **various types of bacteria in the water**, all with extremely strong pathogenicity. Ingesting even a little bit could trigger various fatal diseases.

Sergei watched from afar as the German army frantically transported the sick or dead soldiers, a satisfied smile on his face. He reported via radio:

options.name: “Biological warfare is highly effective. We must rapidly develop more different methods of use.”

title: A Deadly Masterpiece
desc:
Lev used to be an artist, but after his wife and child were lost in the Great War that changed everything, everything changed.

Now, Lev is a glorious Black League soldier, a resolute commander, but at his core, he is still an artist. Next, he will introduce everyone to his most satisfying masterpiece:

"**Poison gas**. Fools regard it as a monstrous flood; they are scared out of their wits just by mentioning it. But we! The great Russians! We see it as a life-saving elixir! The Teutons in the distance are sick, craving to be cured by it. Just a tiny bit will let them be **reborn**!"

"But the great, loving Russians believe a tiny bit is not enough. They will send the **purest and most abundant poison gas** to the poor Teutons! Look, through the yellowish-green veil of the bride, you can see the ecstatic faces of the Teutons! They are overjoyed! They are cheering! They are dancing wildly! In that yellowish-green haze are countless dancers offering us the sincerest gratitude, thanking the Russians for their gift with the wildest dance!"

"Some Teutons are tired and lie down to rest. Look at their lovely, **infant-like faces**! They are sleeping like babies now, and great Russia has become their most loving mother, letting them fully enjoy the hard-won peace amidst the flames of war!"

"It was then that I suddenly recalled the ancient East, a country as old as Russia. It is said that an astonishing art, the '**Jingguan**' (Capital of Skulls), was once practiced there. I find this art to be as beautiful as its name suggests! I could no longer suppress the artistic heart that had been dormant for so long. At that moment, my heart trembled, and my hands wildly shook."

"When I finally completed it, I felt for a moment that **even death would be without regret**. Its structure is extremely simple, or perhaps a little monotonous, but listen, the individual grotesqueries and terror are its best seasoning! They are what give vitality to an otherwise boring scene!"

"I shall name it '**The Roar**,' my deadly masterpiece!"

options.name: A great work of art.

title: Cloudy Liquor
desc:
The cold wind ruthlessly galloped across the Russian land, meeting every attempt to stop it with the most biting rebuff. No one liked this kind of weather, and neither did "Old Dog."

At this moment, he was fumbling his way forward in the heavy snow. He hadn't expected the weather to be so severe today. The muscles on his face had long lost feeling due to the ice and cold wind, only his mouth, still retaining some warmth, occasionally exhaled a brief puff of hot air, reminding him he was still alive.

But his luck wasn't as bad as the weather. After walking for an unknown time in the blizzard, he finally saw the small wooden cabin most familiar to him. He approached the cabin with difficulty, feeling as if with every step, the snow would meticulously cover his previous footprint again. At the door, he reached into his breast pocket and pulled out a string of keys, almost dropping them due to the shaking of his hand, and used them to open the door.

Back inside, "Old Dog" finally felt a hint of relief. He shook the snow off his body and went to the fireplace. The firewood he had started before leaving was still burning a little. So he laboriously stretched out his two hands, which had become red and stiff from the severe cold, trying to rekindle their former vitality with the flames. Gradually, after his hands regained feeling, "Old Dog" took off his wet greatcoat, hung it in front of the fire to dry, and then stood up. He walked to the cabinet, pulled out a bottle of aged liquor, and grabbed a delicate, new-looking glass, which he filled with the liquor. "Old Dog" looked at the ripples forming on the surface of the liquor, watching his face, slightly distorted by the ripples. "The quality of this liquor isn't great," he thought, "but at least it's strong enough. It'll be good for warming up." Just as he was about to down it in one gulp, the door was suddenly kicked open. Startled, he instinctively turned around, only to see two dark gun muzzles pointed at him. He realized that **bandits** had also been driven to his forest cabin by the snowstorm.

"This house belongs to us now, get out!"

"Why can't we live together?"

"How do we know what you'll do in the middle of the night? Stop your fucking nonsense!"

"Old Dog" fell silent. He sighed helplessly and slowly moved towards the door. With every step, he felt the surroundings grow a little darker. "Hurry up, you fucker!" "Old Dog" sped up his pace. When he finally walked outside, just as he was about to turn back for one last look at his old friend, the door was violently slammed shut. "Old Dog" felt enveloped by darkness. He stood frozen in place. But the cold wind, like countless fine needles stabbing his face, his body, and his heart, dragged him out of the endless darkness. Now, "Old Dog" was **homeless**.

options.name: And the glass of cloudy liquor on the table was yet to be drunk.

title: Day After Day
desc:
Smoke rings, obscuring blurred eyes. Alcohol down the throat, numbing a restless heart. No one knew who he was, and no one cared about his story.

He truly could be called a **social parasite**, living only on the occasional goodwill of others. But even so, he still tried his best to scrape a few coins from his daily meager pickings, saving up for a few days to trade for **cigarettes and liquor**, and savoring this hard-won enjoyment. You could often see him quietly smoking or drinking alone, leaning against a wall.

It is said that one day, as he was drinking as usual, a **homeless man** came up and asked him for a drink. Not only did he refuse, but he rudely told the homeless man to scram. Perhaps provoked by his rudeness, the two quickly escalated from a verbal conflict to a physical fight. But he was always malnourished, had a habit of smoking and drinking, and was weak-bodied, so he was quickly defeated, left with a bruised and swollen face. The homeless man snatched his half-bottle of liquor. As for him? He could only pick himself up from the ground, dust himself off, and continue begging for money for the next bottle of liquor. Some say he learned some manners from that fight.

But his life wasn't always so unpleasant. Sometimes, especially on days off, he would go into a small tavern at night, but he didn't have money to buy drinks. He would find an inconspicuous corner and just stand there quietly, listening to the patrons relaxing at the tavern gossiping about people he didn't know. This was the greatest joy he had. But he wasn't just there to listen to stories. He would wait until most people had left and then **collect and drink the leftover liquor** in their glasses. Only this way could he drink some liquors he normally couldn't afford. The owners of the taverns he frequented were mostly accustomed to this and didn't say much to him. So, with half a head full of strange stories and half a head full of mixed liquors, he would stagger out of the tavern, satisfied, find a random spot to sleep, and thus pass the day.

People said he never had any friends, but those who knew him for a long time said this wasn't true. Many years ago, he used to survive with a **young lad**. Back then, he didn't have the habit of smoking and drinking, and his face would sometimes show a smile. Then one day, someone discovered the young lad's **corpse**. Some said the lad starved to death, others that he was beaten to death for stealing, but it no longer mattered. In any case, he picked up smoking and drinking from that day on, and his face always wore a cold, indifferent expression. Some people sympathized with him and tried to give him money, but he always refused back then.

options.name: Thus, day after day, until he stopped appearing.

title: Before the Finality
desc:
Many years have passed since the **Great War** that destroyed the world. With the passage of time, the wounds of the past have gradually been smoothed over, and the survivors hold their heads high, moving forward into the next day.

On the silent Russian land, there are rumors that **Bukharin** is still alive—the man who is believed to be inextricably linked to the Soviet defeat. It is said that he is hiding somewhere deep in the mountains. Some want to find and **put him on trial**; others hope to use him to understand the stories from before the catastrophe, those stories that many have forgotten, as if they never happened. There are also rumors that far in the west, the **Teutons**, who have a blood feud with the Russians, are also alive, but that is too distant and difficult to verify.

One group of people, obsessively promoting their belief, claims that everything humanity has experienced is **God's will**. They refer to the periods before and after the catastrophe as the **Old World** and the **New World**, pointing out that God caused the destruction of the Old World, and they, the humans born in the New World, are **God's messengers**. Their mission is to lead the people of the New World forward, not to repeat the mistakes of the Old World, and to let the New World flourish on the corpses of the Old World. Naturally, there are those who oppose them, claiming that the Old World has not entirely vanished, and many things can prove its existence, and that they are not God's messengers but **complete frauds**.

There is another group of people, the **remnants of the Old World**. Their memories are sealed with the various histories of the past. They cannot accept the fact that they have lost most things. They have either become **mad** or **depressed**. They claim that everything now is fake, is nothingness. They refuse to step out of the bubble of the past. They cannot escape; the past is tightly wrapped around them like chains. They are all people living in the past—people who should have died in the catastrophe.

But everyone in the wasteland, everyone in the New World, without exception, is desperately seeking stories about the catastrophe or the time before it, whether told orally or recorded in documents. They **greedily absorb everything about the past**. They may have smoothed over the old wounds, or perhaps not. All of the past seems to have been torn into thousands of fragments, scattered all over the world. Some were tossed into the sea, never to see the light of day again; some were thrown into magma, turning to dust and scattering to the infinite distance with the wind; and some landed in human hands, becoming known. The past turned into nothingness, and humanity is responsible for filling it, despite the disjointed and chaotic nature of the pieces.

options.name: People constantly explore the stories of the past, piecing together the broken tiles of history.

title: Crime and Punishment
desc:
"Are you sure, beneath here are the Nazis' so-called **graveyards**?" Black League officer Andrei Yubov, leading several soldiers and escorting dozens of German prisoners rounded up from a Nazi settlement, asked the few ragged Ukrainians behind him.

"Yes, General. We used to be **Ukrainian Red Army** soldiers. After our unit was scattered, a few of us, along with our comrades, were taken to this place. The others were killed by them, and the few of us who were lucky enough to survive were captured by these Nazis and used as slaves. A few of our comrades didn't make it and were also persecuted to death by these Nazis."

"Good, let me see!" Yubov turned to look at the men and women behind him, his eyes seeming to erupt with fury. "You dog-fucking Teutonic garbage, **you will immediately dig this place up!** If anyone dares to run, I will shoot you instantly!"

The Germans dared not delay and immediately began working. Yubov handed the Ukrainians a few rifles to supervise. Under their gun barrels, even some German residents who tried to slack off quickly got to work. Soon, amidst a female resident's gasp of surprise, Yubov walked over and saw a **white skeleton** already exposed.

"What are you standing around for? Keep digging along here!"

Soon, a large pit was dug out. Some timid German residents tried to drop their tools and run but were immediately shot. In this large pit, Yubov could see at least **twenty-plus skeletons** with just a glance. He suppressed his discomfort and ordered his soldiers to individually take out the skeletons. During this process, a soldier told him a graver reality.

"You're saying there's an **even bigger pit** right beneath them, and the Nazis killed and buried even more people here?" Yubov looked at the soldier in disbelief.

The soldier nodded. Yubov's hands clenched into fists, and a genuine wave of anger surged into his heart. He looked at the Ukrainians kneeling on the ground, weeping uncontrollably: "Brothers, you have suffered. We will collect the remains of these **Martyrs of the Motherland**."

He turned around, his face ashen, and looked at the shivering Nazi settlers: "As for you, immediately dig another pit. After you're done, **you will voluntarily jump into it!**"

options.name: We will personally punish you for every single blood debt you incurred, one by one!

title: The Net of Heaven and Earth
desc:
"Sir, we are **French *Le Figaro* war correspondents**. We have applied to both the Russian and Greater Germania governments for the right to conduct interviews in this war zone. You cannot illegally arrest us!" "Sir, I am a **businessman from Amsterdam**, here for legal trade. I will protest this illegal arrest of citizens to your Foreign Ministry!" "Sir, as a **Danish citizen**, I strongly protest your illegal arrests and massacres in the foreign residents' quarter!" 
....
"**Shut up! Shut up! You incessantly chattering accomplices!**" As soon as Volkov opened the warehouse door, he saw a pile of people from various countries stand up from the floor, raising all sorts of questions and protesting the "atrocities" of their arrest from the settlement and transport to this so-called temporary prison. Volkov had looked down on these foreigners who came to the Nazi-occupied lands to do "legal business" from the start. Seeing these people now, he couldn't help but pull out his pistol and fire a shot into the ground.

After the gunshot, all the foreigners fell silent, shrinking back. Volkov finally smiled and waved his soldiers into the warehouse.

"Sir, I, representing the **Red Cross** Moscowien branch, protest the persecution of local citizens by the Russian military..."

Volkov's pistol swung around and fired directly at the female representative. "**Good. I knew it. The Nazis can never hide. You scum!**" He pulled out another magazine and reloaded. "I know. You arrogant Europeans have always looked down on us Russians. Look at you—Frenchmen, Danes, Dutchmen, Hungarians—which one of you isn't a **supporter and sympathizer of the Nazis**? You people come to our Motherland's soil, help those damned Nazi invaders, and then rely on your so-called foreign status to suppress the rights of us Russians to survive!" "Sir, we are foreign citizens applying for legal asylum. Does your current statement represent the stance of the Russian government?" "**Foreign citizens? I see no legitimate foreign citizens here, only a bunch of Nazis claiming to be foreigners and then bossing the great Russians around!**" Volkov gave an order, and the soldiers quickly opened fire, killing all these chattering foreigners. He immediately reported this result to his superiors, who quickly sent back a military order.

options.name: All units are notified: any individual claiming to be a national from a non-Teutonic European country or region is to be **immediately executed as a Nazi collaborator**.

title: “Purification is Life”
desc:
Ural Region, "Motherland" Integrated Bunker Complex, Depth: 600m.

The low hum of the ventilation ducts is the eternal main theme of this steel tomb, accompanied by air that has been circulated an untold number of times through the filtration system, the smell of which is indescribable, constantly torturing everyone here. Captain Mikhail pushed open the iron door of the interrogation room, seeing the glaring xenon lamp pour its pale light into every corner, leaving no shadow. The only color in this small room was the huge portrait of **Generalissimo Yazov** hung on the bulletproof panel directly ahead. The intentionally magnified, hawk-like eyes stared intently at the center of the room under the bright lights. Below the portrait, a line of dark red, distorted, and hideous slogan read: "**Declare War on All Corrupt Elements!**"

With his arrival, the three-person team was complete. "**Name!**" Major Petrov, the chief interrogator, began the process. In the defendant's chair, Logistics Lieutenant Semyonov was slumped like a sack of de-boned meat. Mikhail remembered how he looked a month ago when distributing synthetic protein blocks at the rationing station—he could still manage a fake smile then. Now, that lifeless face was only ash-grey.

"**Semyonov Petrovich, Lieutenant, Logistics Support Department, 3rd Food Distribution Station...**" The Major's finger tapped the metal table rhythmically. The recording clerk and the expressionless "**Witness**" (an Interior Ministry agent) were like two statues.

"**Unauthorized appropriation of: 350 kg of Standard Nutrient Paste; 45 liters of High-Efficiency Vitamin D Concentrate; 15 sets of Purified Water Filter Cores...**" The clerk read the list flatly: "**Exchanged through unauthorized channels for: personal entertainment data cards, extra electricity allocation quotas, and...**" The clerk paused, adding without emotion, "**500 milliliters of unapproved strong alcohol.**"

"**The evidence is conclusive!**" The Major suddenly stood up, the metal chair legs scraping the floor with a harsh screech. He pointed at Semyonov, his voice carrying a performative excitement: "**Maggot! Traitor!** The Generalissimo led us through the nuclear blast, through the deathly cold of the surface! Every gram of food, every drop of water, every piece of medicine is what we clawed out of the mud and rock crevices! They are the cornerstone maintaining the last bloodline of Russia! And you!" He spat, "**You are sucking this bloodline! Your greed is stabbing the Generalissimo's heart, stabbing all of our lungs!**"

With a wave of the Major's hand, two "**Purifiers**" stepped out of the shadows and delivered Semyonov to a small side room, which contained a seemingly very old **guillotine**. From the intricate pattern, Mikhail could deduce it was a product of the Russian Empire era. Its blade was still bright and sharp, how many times had it been replaced? He let his mind wander idly while the Major delivered the final judgment on the man's fate: "**The three-person team unanimously rules: Guilt established for Treason and Major Corruption! Highest penalty according to the *Black League Special Period Crime Handling Regulations*! Death! Immediate execution!**"

Semyonov's lips trembled, as if he wanted to say something—perhaps about his wife's worsening radiation sickness? But terror completely sealed his throat. Semyonov couldn't utter a single word.

"*Swish—*" As the blade fell, he would never have the chance to plead his case. And the three judges didn't even bother to say another word.

options.name: After the others left, they casually walked into the revolving door and smoked **cigars not included in the ration**.

title: “Hatred, Without End”
desc:
Samaryov was using a piece of cloth, cut from someone's clothes, to wipe his military knife, which was already dulled from chopping. Hacking down a few disobedient Teutonic beasts, watching the German civilians cry, panic, and run, and then Samaryov gunned them down one by one with his superb marksmanship—such massacres had become his greatest entertainment recently. But suddenly, the sight of a faint German child pulled his thoughts back to the past. In a trance, his mind returned to the past, and the image of Russian children killed, which his teacher had shown him when he was young, overlapped with the present scene.
 
Samaryov, who had been tired, suddenly had his anger rekindled, but now was not the time to erupt, because he thought of a brilliant method of torture....

After confirming that the other person had completely lost consciousness, Samaryov put on a clean shirt, wiped the blood from his body, smoothed his hair, and casually grabbed a bottle of **perfume** from a cosmetics store, spraying half the bottle on himself. Thus, a gentle and refined uncle (at least he thought so) was born.

He gradually woke the little girl, pretending to be afraid, and nervously said to her in German: "Little sister, why are you here alone? It's dangerous. Go find your parents quickly!" 

Hearing this, the little girl's pupils slowly focused, staring straight at him, her voice sobbing: "Uncle, are you... here to save me (sobbing)... My (sobbing) father is gone, and my mother and I are separated... I don't know the address of the 'shelter' she mentioned..." 

Samaryov felt a rush of excitement, but to avoid giving himself away, he suppressed his exhilaration and, through coaxing and deception, got the little girl to tell him the address. Upon reaching the destination and confirming the target through clues, he covered the girl's mouth, slit her throat, and then plunged the knife into her heart. In the girl's desperate eyes, he notified his teammates and guarded the exit closely.

When the sappers opened the door, after a simple **extermination process**, Samaryov was satisfied, gazing for a moment at the sight of the floor covered with purplish corpses and the little girl's expression just before death. Coming back to his senses, he said to himself: "**We are doing the same things that those German beasts did before, but they brought it upon themselves. The Germans proudly killed so many of our compatriots. When they committed their sins, they should have expected a day like this would come.**"

options.name: Then they thoroughly checked, ensuring there were no survivors.

title: Samaryov's Memory
desc:
Inside **Tara City Second Middle School**, 15-year-old Samaryov sat upright. In front of him, the teacher, wearing a black military greatcoat, was lecturing. He was a **West Russian War veteran** with one leg shattered by German shrapnel. His eyes, containing the unextinguished fire of hatred, stared at the students: "Some students might not fully understand why we must completely exterminate the Germans, why we must carry out the Great Trial. After today, such doubts will cease. Because I will answer this question for you."

He opened a large album. The first picture was a cutout from a German newspaper: Russian civilians' corpses piled up like mountains, with a close-up shot of a German officer's smug and bloody smile. The newspaper headline read: **Generalplan Ost is steadily advancing. It is estimated that by 1955, the Reichskommissariat Moskowien will be able to provide approximately 5 million jobs for German civilians.** The next page was an interview with a Russian elder who had escaped from German rule.

"Motherfucker... these beasts..." This was the only thought in Samaryov's mind then, and the subsequent data made him even angrier.

A statistic was shown for the number of Slavs **killed directly by the Germans**; the seven-digit, blood-red number shocked the students... Russians who died in various ways were posted on the Nazi newspaper... The teacher continued: "Those Nazi bastards are **thoroughgoing executioners**. Wherever they go, they kill. Russians, Ukrainians, Belarusians, Latvians, Tatars, Crimeans—they inflicted chemical warfare, biological warfare, and every filthy method in this world upon us. Those pieces of shit even **bombed Russia with their damned planes for nearly 20 years!**" The teacher took a sip of water, then continued to spew his saliva with the force of firing bullets, clearly immersed in his fury: "They only carry out endless destruction and shamelessly claim that their lowly Teutonic bloodline is some **Manifest Destiny**! They are the **maggots of the Earth, the scum of humanity**! Vengeance for hatred, repayment for grievances. Therefore, **Germany must perish!**" The teacher screamed hoarsely, his articulation so powerful that it seemed his words would turn into artillery shells hitting the Germans, as if he were back in the past, a soldier once more...

After class, the children who should have been bustling made no sound, and Samaryov secretly clenched his fists...

options.name: From that moment, he made up his mind.

title: “Wavering”
desc:
Arriving at the concentration camp, Major Viktor pushed open the cell door. What met his eyes were all sorts of faces: some were panic-stricken and full of begging, some were curled up in fear, some were veins-popping with anger, and some were already numb, showing neither joy nor sorrow. He was looking for the first type.

As per routine, he first asked in Finnish: "**Who is willing to serve the Black League?** Those who come forward now can receive preferential treatment and have the opportunity to serve as officials locally. Resistors will be executed."

After a brief silence, the shoulder of a panicking middle-aged man twitched, seemingly wanting to raise his hand. But a young man next to him, whose hands were tied, shoved him hard. Then, the young man shouted ferociously at Viktor: "**You traitor!** The Black League—these beasts worse than pigs and dogs—are invaders, trampling on Finland! They want to destroy Finland! And you, you speak Finnish, yet you help these villains!" Viktor seemed amused and infuriated; he squeezed a contemptuous snort from his nose, then severely slapped the young man: "**I am not Finnish!** I am a Russian violently separated from my motherland by you Finnish pieces of shit! You forced our fathers to fight their own flesh and blood, yet you sit on Russian territory, oppressing our people! I cannot believe you have the audacity to say 'Russia is the invader'?!'"

The young man stared back at him intensely: "If the **Winter War** and what you are doing now are not called invasion, then what is? Finland has always only been defending itself! And your Russian nature is just like this; you are born to be damned invaders and robbers! **Onega and Murmansk** are the interest we rightfully collected for your constant acts of robbery!" Viktor became even angrier. He glared back, unwilling to concede: "Ignorant fool! Finland always wanted more territory! The weak and incompetent Communists ceded Petsamo to you, and in return, you withdrew from **East Karelia**, which should have belonged to Russia, and maintained a constantly **pro-German** attitude throughout the thirties! And 'interest'? By your logic, Finland being completely **exterminated** by Russia is also 'interest'!"

The young man's lips moved a few times, as if he wanted to say something else, but Viktor gagged his mouth and slapped him repeatedly until his own hand was swollen. Viktor finally stopped. He looked contemptuously at the young man's furious and mortified expression, brutally crushed his face with his long boot until it was bloody, clapped his hands, and said: "**Guard, take this stubborn element out and shoot him!** Alright, is anyone else willing to defect now?"

options.name: **Five** people gradually raised their hands.

title: No Sanctuary Left
desc:
Karl Stein knocked on the disguised bunker door with a secret signal. The door quickly opened a crack, and he swiftly slipped inside. Afterwards, the scene looked as if nothing had happened.

"**Look what I found! A whole box of old canned tomatoes! And a huge pile of potatoes!**" Karl's smile looked somewhat distorted, and despite the slightly menacing, tattered gas mask, his excitement was clearly visible. The survivors in the shelter all gathered around: his emaciated wife, his child who was thin as a ghost, old Schroeder who had lung disease from inhaling large amounts of residual poison gas a decade ago, assembly line worker Schmidt... A relaxed and joyful atmosphere permeated the group, and people whispered, enjoying the rare good news.

Karl used his already cracked fingers to carefully pull out a **malformed potato**—affected by radiation—from the fire. He peeled off the thick, warty skin. Although the thing looked ominous and tasted and smelled terrible, it was at least an edible crop.

The light flickered on and off. Hank the electrician frowned and went to check the only light source deep inside their bunker—a small lightbulb connected to a discarded car battery in the corner. In the past, they wouldn't have even glanced at such an old incandescent bulb, but now it had become a rare treasure in the heap of junk.

The water boiled. Karl put some kind of **mutated fungus** and a large piece of unusually overgrown **moss** into an empty tin can along with the potato. Within minutes, the mixture turned into a paste-like, deep-green thin soup. A strong fishy/gamey smell, the fragrance of starch mixed with a faint stench of decay, permeated the air. This was all the food they had for tonight—Karl wished he could break even this stuff in half. Now, their water resources had run out. All the clean water sources within a ten-mile radius had long been occupied by the remaining government organizations, and they simply couldn't afford the water collection fees... In silence, the group slept facing each other.

The next morning, Karl put on the gas mask that always made his breathing difficult, wrapped himself in three layers of tattered cloth that served as a makeshift protective suit, and set off again. However, as he walked, he gradually felt something was wrong. The ground was shaking, and the movement grew louder and louder. There was no time to think; he immediately ran towards the bunker. But when he climbed the small hill that was a necessary path, a hellish scene came into view: dozens of **camouflaged armored vehicles**, painted with thick anti-radiation layers and fully armed. "This can't be the government; they don't have this kind of power... Then, could it be..." A terrifying guess surfaced. He risked his life to get closer and observe these steel behemoths. Fortunately, the observers on top didn't spot him, but when he realized the truth of the matter, he felt he'd be better off dead:

options.name: The emblem on the armored vehicles was a **white double-headed eagle**.

title: The Final Military Order
desc:
Dudayev and Sergei, wearing thick anti-radiation masks, led an entire team of agents forward. After the Alliance High Command began gradually establishing contact with surrounding regions, Dudayev's agent team was dispatched westward. The order he received here was to link up with the **Russian forces in the Moscow area**. The mission brief stated that after the Great Trial, the Alliance had sent a force toward Moscow, advancing into Teutonic territory to kill all remaining Nazis. But since their dispatch, this force had been silent. To ensure the ultimate success of the Great Trial, contact *must* be immediately established with the Moscow garrison. Therefore, Dudayev and his team were sent toward Moscow, and if possible, to bring back **Yevgeny Savintsev**, one of the Alliance High Command members.

Reassuringly, the team quickly found the **Black League's exclusive internal signal**.

"Old brother, do we have enough supplies?" Sergei looked at Dudayev; through the small observation window, he clearly saw a hint of hesitation: "Little brother, why do you ask? The supplies arranged by the High Command are enough to resettle several more people."

Dudayev said nothing, and Sergei also felt uneasy. The two continued leading the team toward the source of the signal. After a small-scale search, the team found a house. After confirming it was the source of the signal, Dudayev led the way, and the Alliance team kicked open the door of the room, on whose wall was written: **Moscow Supreme Military Command Post**. Behind the door, they saw a soldier, also wearing black clothes, looking emaciated like a skeleton. Even after all of them entered, the soldier just sat blankly in his chair, making no move.

"Hey, soldier, we are Russian Government Revival Team No. 15. Are you from the Moscow Army Group?" "Ah, ah, time to **defend Moscow**." The soldier suddenly stood up stiffly, speaking in barely coherent fragments. "Brother, the Commander has given the order. Get your weapons immediately and defend Moscow."

"Where is Commander Yevgeny? Where did he go?" "Commander? Yes, must find the Commander." Following the soldier, the team found a room. Looking around, there were **white skeletons everywhere**. The soldier, however, pulled out a radio and started dialing. Soon, a familiar message came from the radio: "**According to the Generalissimo's directive, all cadres and soldiers, please hold your posts and await the conclusion of the Great Trial!**"

The two looked at each other, understanding instantly. Dudayev gave the final order. "Soldier, the Alliance has confirmed that the **Battle of Moscow is successfully concluded**. Army Group Commander Yevgeny Savintsev **died heroically** in the defense of Moscow. Your duty is over."

Hearing this, the soldier suddenly froze, then collapsed straight to the floor, lifeless. The two hurried to move whatever usable items they could from the command post. As they were leaving, Sergei looked at the radio on the desk, which was still broadcasting automatically, silently switched it off. Then, he and the team left without looking back.

options.name: After today, the night sky over Moscow is silent.

title: Cardiac Arrest, Once More
desc:
Germania's lead-grey sky was like a thick blanket, tightly wrapping the earth. The suspended dust had not dissipated for decades. This once great city was practically extinct. No meaningful human activity could take place here, and the barely surviving **German State** could only continue to use it as the nominal capital—that was the most they could do. Heinrich Müller stood on the cold concrete steps guarding the bunker door. His life here was also lead-grey, unchanged for decades—searching for all sorts of things, or people, and guarding the bunker. But everyone understood that "guarding" was only against bandits and vagrants. As for a regular military force... He hadn't had time to think further when a sound he thought he had long forgotten tore through the bunker's silence—the **air raid siren**, a remnant of the old era that still functioned somewhat! Heinrich's heart felt gripped by a cold hand, instantly stopping its beat. Following that came the heavy, rhythmic, metallic echoing thud of footsteps, approaching from the ruins overhead, getting closer and louder—a sound he was equally familiar with: **long boots**. He had heard this sound countless times when he served in the Wehrmacht. Despair enveloped his heart. He had heard rumors about the Black League a long time ago, and news of the front-line declaration of war had reached his ears early on, but he hadn't cared. After all, what could an old man with one foot in the grave do? And now... he feared he wouldn't have a good end.

"**Boom!**" With a loud bang, the heavy metal plate sealing the entrance was violently **blown open**. The blinding white beam of a flashlight violently pierced the dimly lit bunker, and dust danced wildly in the light column. The choking smell of gunpowder smoke mixed with an even more pungent chemical odor surged in. Deep-grey figures emerged like specters from hell, wearing **gas masks**, their eyes behind the lenses devoid of emotion. The intruders, Black League soldiers, immediately secured the area. Rifle butts ruthlessly smashed into everyone who tried to retreat, and the sound of cracking bone and screams echoed in the bunker's narrow confines. The soldiers herded the shrinking crowd toward the blasted hole with their gun muzzles, like driving cattle. Heinrich was brutally shoved, stumbling up the pile of rubble.

Outside was the lead-grey, perpetually gloomy sky. The biting cold wind whipped his exposed cheeks. The sight before him made his stomach churn: lines of emaciated, hollow-eyed German survivors, brutally shoved and beaten at bayonet and whip point, were being organized into long queues. Cries, curses, and the dull thud of rifle butts hitting flesh merged into a suffocating marching tune.

A soldier brutally grabbed Heinrich's arm, dragging him away from the crowd. Another soldier, the eagle on his arm flashing cold light, picked up a **sprayer** and sprayed the sticky, strong-smelling, disinfectant-like **deep-green liquid** all over Heinrich's head and face. The liquid stung his skin and burned his eyes.

"**Pig, count yourself lucky**," the spraying soldier mocked in Russian, his voice buzzing through the gas mask, "**'Purification' complete. Now, to the mine! Dig out the last bit of value from your land for the Black League!**" He shoved Heinrich toward another group of people, carrying simple mining picks and walking toward a huge **open-pit mine** in the distance. On the edge of the mine, a massive **black flag** flapped violently in the radiation wind, like a majestic eagle that had captured its prey, overlooking the German slaves, who were as small as ants at its feet.

options.name: Don't think that a trip through hell will be enough to clear the sins you have committed.

title: “Rot”
desc:
Kuznetsov, or Agent 350234, as a member of the Alliance Central Administration's special anti-corruption inspection team, had been dispatched to **Krasnoyarsk** for three days. He had gathered clues about **systemic corruption** in the local bureaucracy through secret channels, but their investigation faced heavy resistance, as if he were not eliminating Russia's internal pests but fighting against the entire Alliance.

....

At **Lead Mine No. 3**, the mine manager, a Colonel whose face was etched with the marks of time and whose eyes were as murky as an underground river, slowly flipped through the documents and said: "Comrade Special Commissioner, unfortunately, the main lift shaft is undergoing routine pressure maintenance and has been forcibly shut down for forty-eight hours. Safety regulations, you understand?" Kuznetsov requested to walk down, but the man merely spread his calloused hands: "The dust concentration below is excessive, and it's a **strong radiation residual zone**. Without professional protective equipment, going down alone puts you at extreme risk of radiation sickness. The equipment... regrettably, was just sent to the 'Central Maintenance Station' for servicing." Kuznetsov sneered, continuing to press, but all he received was a volley of slippery, non-committal nonsense that gave him nothing to grip. The two batted the issue back and forth for half an hour, yet Kuznetsov made zero progress. He had to temporarily set this aside and headed to the archive database, but when he requested to check the accounts, the archive manager apologized: "We are very sorry, Comrade Special Commissioner, but the system is undergoing 'Critical Data Migration.' Historical records are temporarily... well, in a **locked state** and inaccessible. Expected to be recovered in one week." "**One week?!** You motherfucking..." Kuznetsov felt a wave of chilling, violent emotion surge from his soles straight to the top of his head. The subservient response of the shifty-eyed man only further ignited the fire in his heart. He glared heavily at the man, threatening: "**You better not expose yourselves.**" The reply was: "You shouldn't speak like that, Comrade Special Commissioner. You mustn't wrongly accuse good people!" Kuznetsov angrily rushed to the Mayor's office, explaining the suspicious situation to **Mayor Glebov**, who widened his eyes and thumped his chest, assuring "**full cooperation**." However, whenever Kuznetsov needed *substantive* support—such as a reliable squad of guards to raid a suspicious warehouse, or the mandatory retrieval of a key figure's communication records—Glebov was *always* "coincidentally" absent. His deputy, a Captain with a perpetually professional smile, became the perfect buffer. "The Lieutenant Colonel is hosting an urgent defense meeting, Comrade Special Commissioner. It's very important, concerning deep rock stress monitoring..." "The clearance you need? Oh, that requires cross-verification from the local Security Committee. The process might take a while..." A smile, an apology, and **delay**. All his efforts were like punching a water-soaked cotton quilt—silent, and achieving nothing.

....

"**Conclusion: Investigation shows that the logistics management in the Krasnoyarsk region contains certain technical omissions, and relevant personnel exhibit insufficient vigilance. A verbal warning has been issued. No evidence of systemic corruption was found. Recommendation: Strengthen ideological education.**" As these large words concluded the report, Kuznetsov finally slumped, leaning back weakly into his seat. Two full weeks had passed. He was scheduled to start his journey back tomorrow, but he... Kuznetsov stared blankly at the "**Special Investigation Authorization**" on his hand, which bore the **blood-red seal of Supreme Commander Marshal Yazov from Omsk**. At this moment, it felt like a burning brand, searing his fingertips, yet chilling his heart—**it was worthless here**. Kuznetsov angrily slammed the desk, the loud *thud* resonating. The guard outside the soundproof door seemed to sense something, turned back, and gave him a smile. Kuznetsov felt the smile was not meant as goodwill but as **silent mockery**.

options.name: Damn it, this hellhole is rotten to the core...

title: Pulling the Radish, Bringing Out the Mud
desc:
“Knock, knock, knock”

Yazov's office received another visitor. The guards brought in Agent 350234, namely Kuznetsov.

Looking at the middle-aged man who seemed vaguely familiar, Yazov paused to recall his identity—the man had once been a district-level cadre in Omsk’s Ministry of Internal Affairs. Due to his exceptional ability and meticulous logic, Yazov had exceptionally promoted him to Lieutenant Colonel, reporting directly to him. He remembered having dispatched him to the Krasnoyarsk region for an anti-corruption investigation. Stopping his train of thought, Yazov pointed to the opposite chair, signaling for him to sit down.

“What are the results of the investigation?”

“It’s rotten, Comrade Commander-in-Chief... The situation in the Minusinsk bunker complex, where you sent me, is seriously amiss. But when I requested to look up certain data, or to investigate departments where corruption might exist, everyone—from grassroots staff to module supervisors—was stalling, misleading, and subjected us to information lockdown and comprehensive surveillance. There were even instances of data mysteriously disappearing and key witnesses dying in ‘accidents’... The resistance we faced is not isolated; this is absolutely a vast network of connections. They’ve done an excellent job of covering their tracks, and we haven't found any decisive evidence on the surface. I suspect there are monumental problems involved... but I am unable to uncover them... Marshal Comrade, I need you to send more elite, trustworthy MVD assault teams, grant me the highest authority across regions and hierarchies, and give me direct, real-time communication access to you.”

Upon hearing this, Yazov’s face turned grim, like still water. His body leaned slightly forward, fingertips constantly tapping the armrest, and he scrutinized Kuznetsov with an icy gaze. After a long silence, he finally spoke: “Agent 350234, are you sure you can be responsible for your words? You must know that if this is true, the implications are incredibly deep. Other investigators haven’t reported any problems. How am I to believe you?”

Kuznetsov took a deep breath, meeting Yazov’s eyes and sensing the brewing storm within him: “Comrade Commander-in-Chief, I am willing to bear all responsibility. As for credibility, I have some personal intelligence here. I ask you to review it.”

...As he read, the air around Yazov seemed to solidify. He frowned: “Are you certain that even parts of the MVD organs in these areas have been compromised? How did you get this information? Why is your intelligence more timely than that of my intelligence agencies?”

“Comrade Commander-in-Chief, I have some acquaintances in these places. They were personally involved in this corruption network, and I successfully turned them using your name without prior authorization, which is why you are able to see this document... Rest assured, this information is absolutely reliable.” Yazov rubbed his temples, pondering for a long time. Finally, he made a decision: “Fine, I will grant your request. But if there is no result in the end... you know what your fate will be.” Kuznetsov felt his voice was as low as thunder, but surprisingly, the voice of the man of steel even carried a hint of... trembling? He could faintly discern it.

options.name: Kuznetsov secretly wondered, “Is he afraid?”

title: The Rotten Fruit of Bitterness
desc:
